## 1. THE BUCKET IS HIDDEN — ONE CONSTANT, ONE FILTER

New **`HIDE_UNFAMILIED = true`** beside `NO_ZONE` in `AuctionApp.kt`, applied at the single point where the mob browser derives its list:

```kotlin
val mobList = ui.mobResults
    .let { if (HIDE_UNFAMILIED && ui.query.isBlank()) it.filter { m -> m.family.isNotBlank() } else it }
    .let { if (ui.mobFilter == "nm") it.filter { m -> m.nm } else it }
```

306. **ONE LIST FEEDS ALL FOUR MOB VIEWS, SO ONE FILTER HIDES THE BUCKET EVERYWHERE.** `fam == ""` was surfacing in **five** places, not one — `Other > Unknown` in the Family view, and an `Unknown` sub-group inside every Zone group, the NO_ZONE group, and every Content group. All five read `mobList`. **Nothing was renamed, no group was special-cased, and the five `ifBlank { "Unknown" }` call sites are untouched** — they simply have nothing to catch while browsing. Had this been fixed at the group level it would have been five edits and five chances to miss one.

**IT IS A BROWSE FILTER, NOT A DATA CHANGE.** mobs.json is untouched by it, and **the filter is skipped whenever a search query is active** — `mobResults` is `mobDb.all()` when the query is blank and `mobDb.search(q)` when it is not, so typing a name still reaches every one of the 374. The pile is invisible while browsing and one query away when you want it, which is what keeps the research loop working. **`false` brings the whole bucket back.**

### Not filtered, on purpose — say the word if you want it extended

The **Content tab** (`mobsForContent`) and the Apex/Locus rosters (`mobsByNamePrefix`) call `mobDb.all()` directly and were left alone. Dropping a real mob out of a Dynamis-D roster to tidy a bucket makes the roster silently wrong, which is worse than the tidying. **The exposure is exactly six records:**

| tab | records |
|---|---|
| Dynamis D | `commander's pet`, `volte's pet` |
| Master Trials | `lilisette`, `lion`, `prishe` |
| Unity | `kanavid` |

## 3. det policy, written down

Four more corrections — `jotunn ruffian`, `kalos eunomia`, `inquisitor mortuus`, `harpimaira`, all the `[Sight, …, True Sight]` shape, **sixteen records in four revs.** The rule the last three revs have actually been following, now stated in the script header:

> **The page's notes-column letters REPLACE `det`, with one carve-out: `Blood` survives where the record already carries it.** HP is the flag editors most often omit, and 510 records file-wide have it. Everything else the page does not print is dropped.

That is why `inquisitor mortuus` kept Blood and `kalos eunomia` lost `Magic`.

299. **THE `X's pet` SHAPE RESOLVES TO THE PET'S OWN FAMILY — AND WE ALREADY HAVE A FAMILY FOR IT.** Rev 141 held nine literal name matches back because the head noun disagreed with the family word, and rev 346 warned not to one-script them. ## What the X is, from rev 141

USER, 2026-07-23: *"go through the rest of the unknown section and move mobs that look like they should be somewhere else. no guesses, but things like rabbit should go in rabbit. mark these with the x icon here so i can look at them later."*

138 orphans were folded into 56 existing families and each was stamped with `mobimages/review_x.png` as its **per-mob `img`**. `iconForMob` is per-mob img > family icon, so the X beats the family icon and none of them can be missed in the browser. **They are not in the bucket** — every one has a family — which is why they had fallen out of the review entirely and needed their own section.

**The rule was literal, not inferred:** a record moved only if its own name contains an existing family name **as a whole word**, last match winning (`naraka bat` → Bat, not Naraka). A statistical trailing-token rule was built first and thrown away — it produced `aquarian caster` → Scorpion, `goblin duelist` → Orc and similar, each off one coincidental co-occurrence.

**Nine literal matches were hand-excluded** — the family word is in the name but the head noun says otherwise (the `X's pet` shape: `vampyr wolf` is not a Vampyr). **Those nine are still orphans, and they are exactly what Section 3 of the report is showing today** — `vampyr bats`, `vampyr wolf`, `poroggo's toady`, `muut's hound warrior`, `savage hound condottiere`, `dragzagg's wyvern`, `eschan il'aern's spirit`, `cardian prototype`, plus the toads. Section 3's 12 records are the residue of that hand-exclusion, not a fresh pile.

## The section

Grouped by the family each record was moved INTO, largest first — Goblin 14, Demon 10, Gigas 9, Bat 8, Flock Bat 8, Acuex 7, down to 30 families holding one each. Reviewing by destination family is the useful order: a wrong call shows up as one odd name in an otherwise coherent list.

**Undo is still one line** — clear `img` wherever it equals that path and all 138 fall back to their family icon. **None of them had art to lose**, verified before the marker was written.

**Rev 345 — 2026-07-27. UI only, no data touched. One colour for every tab's top level, and the Trusts roster folded under a single collapsed section. USER: "Top level of each tab needs to be the same color, some are white, some gold. Trusts need a collapsed section in tab that they all fall under."** mobs.json UNCHANGED (6972 / 433 orphans); audit §2 ALL 0. AWAITING COMPILE.

## 1. Why three tabs drifted white

`Color.kt` already declares the tier — `HeaderL1 = AccentGold` with the comment *"every TOP-LEVEL heading in every tab uses HeaderL1"* — and every tab whose top level is a **group** goes through `GroupHeader`, which honours it. The three tabs whose top level is a **flat menu** had no header composable to go through, so each hand-rolled a `Text` row and picked `TextSoft`:

- **Jobs** — the 22 job rows
- **Content** — the 13 content-type rows
- **Chains** — the "Weapon Skills" reference link (rev 338), which was also a `Surface` card rather than a row

297. **A COLOUR CONSTANT DOES NOT ENFORCE ITSELF — A SHARED COMPOSABLE DOES.** The tier comment has been in `Color.kt` for revs and three menus still drifted, because nothing made them route through it. New **`TopLevelRow(label, enabled, trailing, subtitle, insetDp, onClick)`** is now the only way to draw a flat level-1 entry; `GroupHeader` covers the grouped case. **Anything at level 1 goes through one of those two.** `TopLevelRow` also carries the disabled state (Content's "Soon" rows stay muted with the tag on the right) and an `insetDp` escape hatch, because the Chains column already pads 16dp and would otherwise double it.

**Untouched on purpose:** data rows stay `TextSoft` — item results, `MobRow`, `ZoneRow`, `TrustRow`. The complaint was about level-1 *navigation*, and making 6,972 mob names gold would erase the distinction between a heading and a record.

## 2. Trusts: one section over the whole roster

The tab opened on seven role headers stacked under the reference sections. Now the roster sits under a **single top-level "Alter Egos" section, collapsed by default, with the total (122) on the right**; the seven roles drop to level 2 (`SubGroupHeader` / `HeaderL2` blue) inside it. Same shape the Content tab took at rev 219 when the area groups moved inside "Zones".

**The body stays LAZY.** `CollapsibleSection` takes a content lambda, which would have realised all 122 trust rows at once, so the header was split out as **`SectionToggleRow(title, expanded, count, onClick)`** — pixel-identical to `CollapsibleSection`'s header row, but usable as a `LazyColumn` item with the roles emitted conditionally after it. **Use it whenever a collapsible section wraps a long list.**

The Trusts tab now reads: five reference sections, then Alter Egos — six level-1 headings, all gold, all collapsed.

zoneinfo stores those tables in a **`geasfete`** key, beside `nms` and `mobs`, and it is complete: **ZiTah 12/6/3/4 · RuAun 12/6/3/5/6/11 · Reisenjima 12/6/3/7 — every group, every row, with the tier titles in a `t` field and the Zone screen already rendering them.** I printed `len(nms)` and `len(mobs)`, saw the shortfall, and never listed the keys.

**Rules 262 and 266 are retired.** The lesson is the one rule 244 already taught in a different costume: **a result that says an established file is missing a large, coherent block is a bug in my query first and a finding second — list the keys before counting them.** Nothing was written on the strength of the wrong claim, so there is nothing to undo in the data.

## 1. The ` (monster)` suffix is gone

**USER: "only nms get '(NM)' appending their name if we have duplicate names, monsters are left alone."**

Twenty-two records ended in ` (monster)`. Looking at them side by side, **twenty-one are not two mobs at all — they are two imports of one mob.** Every base-side record has the same shape (`fam: None`, no ability list, the old half-tier `+25%/-50%` grid, `agg`/`lnk`/`resp`) and every twin has the bestiary family pass's shape (family set, full kit, `job`, `crys`, `img`, the `+30%/-40%` grid). That is why rule 246's census came out 17-3: **whichever side a project touched first got the data.**

**Those 21 merged into the plain name.** The surviving record is whichever side held more zones (ties by key count); everything the survivor lacked was folded in from the other side; `zones`, `lv` and `notes` were unioned; and **every field where the two disagreed is printed in the script's output** so nothing vanished quietly. Highlights:

- **`gessho`** kept its eleven ninjutsu moves over the twin's five-move bird kit — the twin had been family-stamped wrong.
- **`gnole`** took the twin's `job: Monk` over the base's `Warrior`; **`odontotyrannus`** kept the base's quest spawn, drops and `nmlv` on top of the twin's Pugil kit.
- **`antares`**' note "Likely duplicate of Antares (Monster)." was dropped — it was provenance prose in a player-facing field, which §5's first rule forbids.

**The one genuine collision is `siren`:** the base was the **Avatar** (`siren prime.png`) and the twin a **Lesser Bird**. Per your rule the monster keeps the bare name, so `siren` is now the bird and the avatar moved to `siren (nm)` / "Siren (NM)".

**And that turned up something I should have checked first: a ` (nm)` convention already exists, 23 records of it — `siren (nm)` was already there.** My write clobbered the stub before I caught it in the key diff; it is restored (its `job: BLM / BRD` is back on the merged record). **The key-count diff is what caught it — 7031 minus 22 is 7009, not 7010, and that one missing record was the whole story.**

Five zoneinfo rows spelled `X (Monster)` (three Grenades, a Chigoe, a Condor) were renamed to match.

## 2. The ` (nm)` class needs the same pass — here is what it looks like

Since your rule governs both suffixes, I audited the 23 existing `(nm)` records against it:

- **Three have no plain twin at all** — `belladonna (nm)`, `chaos (nm)`, `harpeia (nm)`. There is no duplicate name, so **the suffix is doing nothing** and they should drop it.
- **Seven are core-identical to their plain twin** (`brunhilde`, `flesh eater`, `gold quadav`, `iron quadav`, `mamool ja`, `poroggo`, `silver quadav`) — same family, kit, grid and art. **Same duplicate-import shape as the 21 above; they want merging.**
- **The rest are real collisions and correctly suffixed** — `nergal (nm)` is a Demon against a Leech, `siren (nm)` an Avatar against a Lesser Bird, and the Avatar pairs (`alexander`, `bahamut`, `odin`, `atomos`) separate the summon from the NM.

**Ten of twenty-three want changing. Nothing done — say the word.**

The floor-layout table lists **41 distinct mobs and all 41 have records.** Per your instruction I added the zone only to the ones carrying no zones at all: **`kulshedra`, `manticore` and `bull bugard`.** The other 38 already hold zones and were left alone — **but the table is a membership statement, so if you want Nyzul Isle on all 41, that is one line.** Holders 35 → 38.

**96 NMs tagged** `Geas Fete: <zone>: <group>` across the three zones: Zi'Tah 25, Ru'Aun 43, Reisenjima 28, split Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 / HELM / Ark Angels / Heavenly Beasts / Nazar.

## 3. !!!! `pallas (s)` — A PARKED SHARED-KEY COLLISION THAT WAS ALREADY SOLVED

Vunkerl's NM table prints **`Pallas` at 83**, and `Pallas` is one of the **ten parked shared-key collisions** from the zone-intake project. The bare record is the **Upper Delkfutt's Tower** Gigas: `lv [72,72]`, forced spawn by trading a Hoary Battle Horn, one zone.

**A second record exists — `pallas (s)` — holding `Vunkerl Inlet [S]` at exactly 83, and nothing else.** The collision was split into two records at some earlier point and nobody wrote it down. **The row went to `pallas (s)`; the bare `pallas` was not touched.**

**There is a whole ` (s)` disambiguator class and it has exactly four members**: `pallas (s)`, `de'vyu headhunter (s)`, `kingslayer doggvdegg (s)`, `shadow lord (s)`. **It is the same device as ` (monster)` — BG's own suffix for a name collision, inherited by our keys — and `de'vyu headhunter (s)` is one of the six Bucket-E entries I flagged at Beadeaux two revs ago as a mysterious "apostrophe-named court NM".** It was not mysterious; it was an `(s)` twin doing its job. **Check for a ` (s)` sibling before treating any [S]-zone NM row as a collision.**

## 4. Rule 237 confirmed, and a sub-rule it needed

**`Dark Ixion`**: the page publishes **`80+`** and we already store **`80-85`** for this zone (and for its other six). Kept ours — that is rule 237 exactly, and it is now confirmed rather than proposed.

**`Sandworm`** gave the sub-rule. Its Rolanberry entry had no level, so `80+` was written verbatim (rule 11) — **but the union code then tried to widen its global `lv` from `[85,88]` down to `[80,88]`, because `band('80+')` reads the floor as a minimum.** That is backwards: **`N+` is an open-ended FLOOR, not a measured band, and trading a measured 85-88 for it loses information.** The script now returns early on any `+` string before the union. **Caught in the dry run, nothing shipped.**

## 5. The same NM, two different bands, two sibling [S] pages

`Sandworm` holds seven [S] zones. **Four of them store `~88` from their own pages; this page publishes `80+`.** Both are stored verbatim, so the record now carries two different published bands for one timed spawn that is the same mob everywhere.

**This is a new shape of page disagreement** — not zoneinfo vs the page (rule 242's three shapes), but **page vs page.** Nothing is wrong in the file; it is just worth knowing that verbatim storage means a mob's zone bands are not comparable across zones unless the pages agree.

## 1. !!!! A ZONE-STRING NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT BEFORE IT REACHED THE FILE

My first comparison ran against **`Crawlers' Nest [S]`** — with an apostrophe — and came back with **zero records holding the zone and an empty Bucket E**, i.e. "36 zone adds, the biggest single-zone result of the sweep."

**It was the wrong string.** zones.json spells it **`Crawlers Nest [S]`**, no apostrophe, and **41 records already hold it.** The zone was well covered; I had simply typed the English possessive.

Nothing was written from the bad comparison, but it is the third time an apostrophe has bitten this sweep — after `Outer RaKaznar` (rev 318) and `Ghoyus Reverie` (rev 321), both of which zones.json also spells bare. **The habit that catches it: read the canonical spelling out of zones.json before running the comparison, not after.** A result that says "an entire established zone has no coverage" should be treated as a bug in my query first and a finding second.

## 2. Twenty fills — the most of any rev — and sixteen of them are one block

**11 zone adds · 20 fills · 4 corrections · 3 rule-9 unions · 16 `lv` sets.**

**Crawlers Nest [S] carries a sixteen-row Apex/Locus block at levels 129-140**, and every one of them already held the zone with **no level and no `lv` at all**. The page publishes a band for all sixteen, in a clean ladder: Lugcrawler 129-131 → Hornfly 131-133 → Worker Lugcrawler / Nest Elytra 132-134 → Dragonfly 133-135 → Soldier Lugcrawler / Blazer Elytra 134-136 → Mycelar / Rumble Lugcrawler / Helm Elytra / Doom Scorpion 136-138 → Lugcrawler Hunter 137-139 → **Knight Lugcrawler 138-140**, plus the two Apex Elementals at 132-135.

**These sixteen were the emptiest records the sweep has touched** — a name, a family, one zone and nothing else.

## 3. A new action: `lv` set where a record had none

Those same sixteen had **no `lv` field**, so the mob card showed no level anywhere. **Each holds exactly one zone — this one — so the zone's published band IS its global band, with nothing to infer.**

I set `lv` on all sixteen from the page. **This is additive in the strict sense: the script asserts `'lv' not in mob` before writing and asserts the record has exactly one zone entry, which is this page's.** No existing value could be touched even by accident.

**It is a genuinely new action for this phase**, which until now only ever *extended* an existing `lv` (rule 9). Filling a missing one is squarely inside the phase's "zones + levels" remit and is a one-line revert if you disagree — **but say so and I will not do it again without asking.**

**Four Adoulin-era zones, four pages that publish a complete roster and almost no levels.** This is not a capture problem and it is not a gap in our data — the wiki simply does not carry levels for this content the way it does for the classic zones. **Expect bare zone adds, not fills, on every remaining Ulbuka page**, and do not read a blank cell as a hole to be filled later.

## !!!! A BLANK GENUS CELL IDENTIFIES A TERRAIN HAZARD

Five rows across the two pages have **no Genus at all**: `Numbing Blossom` on Yahse, and `Erupting Geyser`, `Knotted Root`, `Nachtschatten` and `Pungent Fungus` on Moh Gates. **Four of the five are not mobs in our file** — they are the established hazard families under eco `Structures`:

- `erupting geyser` and `pungent fungus` → **`fam=Environment`** (4 members file-wide)
- `knotted root` → **`fam=Obstacle`** (6 members file-wide)
- `numbing blossom` → **`fam=None`**

The fifth, `nachtschatten`, is a genuine `fam=Mandragora`. So the correlation is not perfect — but it is strong enough to be useful in the other direction, and it **retro-classifies an orphan**: `numbing blossom` matches `pungent fungus` **field for field** — `lv [1,1]`, `nm: true`, `agg: true`, `det: ["Sound"]` — which is the signature of a hazard, not of a mob missing its family.

**Not applied** ((ky) precedent: a family fold is a family-pass action). But it is worth flagging that this is **the strongest fold evidence the sweep has produced**: every previous candidate rested on a single Genus cell that could be a rule-5 copy error, whereas this one rests on a blank Genus *plus* a complete profile match with a confirmed member of the family being proposed. **One word folds it.**

## The Sortie Maps section — what changed

**Two new assets**, bundled at 2048×2048 as supplied (~840 KB each, 1.7 MB total):
`assets/contentmaps/sortie_top.jpg` and `assets/contentmaps/sortie_bottom.jpg`. **`contentmaps/` is a new folder** deliberately kept separate from `assets/maps/`, whose README reserves that directory for FFXI map-pack files named `<zoneID-hex>_<index>` — these are composite content maps, not zone maps, and putting them in `maps/` would break that contract.

**Four Kotlin edits, all in `AuctionApp.kt`:**
- `SortieScreen` gains a **"Maps" CollapsibleSection at the top of the body**, above Overview, plus local `openMap` state, a `BackHandler(enabled = openMap != null)`, and a `Box` wrapper so the viewer can overlay the list.
- The top bar now shows the open map's title and its back arrow closes the map before leaving Sortie.
- New private `SortieMap` class + `SORTIE_MAPS` list — **the top map is the Ground Floor (sectors A-D, with Ghatjot / Leshonn / Skomora / Degei) and the bottom is the Basement (E-H, with Dhartok / Gartell / Triboulex / Aita plus Aminon)**, which is exactly how the existing "Sectors & Foes" section already splits them, so the two agree.
- New `SortieMapRow` and `SortieMapOverlay`. **The overlay reuses the existing private `ZoomableImage`** — the same pinch-to-zoom / drag-to-pan composable the zone map viewer uses — so tapping a row opens it full screen with the behaviour you already know from Zones.

**Verification done in place of a compile** (I still cannot build Kotlin here): every identifier used was grepped against the file first — `BackHandler`, `background`, `clickable`, `clipToBounds`, `BitmapFactory`, `asImageBitmap`, `LocalContext`, `HorizontalDivider`, `FontWeight.SemiBold`, `AccentGold`, `TextSoft`, `TextMuted`, `CharcoalDark`, `Charcoal` are all already imported or in use; `androidx.compose.runtime.*` covers the `by remember { mutableStateOf(...) }` delegate. **`SortieMap` / `SORTIE_MAPS` / `SortieMapRow` / `SortieMapOverlay` were checked for name collisions across the whole module and are unique** (rule 14's lesson, applied outside `ZoneInfoDb`). Brace, paren and bracket balance re-checked file-wide after the edit: 1768/1768, 5029/5029, 63/63. `SortieScreen` opens and closes cleanly at lines 2057-2223.

## The Apex Archaic Cog(s) pair — bucket E again, and a new twin axis

The Alzadaal page publishes **two** Adversaries rows for Apex Archaic Cogs, at **142-145** and **146-147**. The file has **two records**: `apex archaic cog` (singular, 143-145) and `apex archaic cogs` (plural, 146-147). zoneinfo merged the rows into a single `142-147`.

**The twin check missed this — singular/plural is another axis the normalized key cannot see** (`apexarchaiccog` vs `apexarchaiccogs`), and the suffix probe does not apply either. **Bucket E caught it.**

**Not merged, and here is why.** I pixel-measured both name cells: **82px and 81px** — a sub-character difference, where rule 105's Tracer/Tracker pair differed by a whole letter blob. So both page rows really do print the same string. **But the two records carry DIFFERENT accuracy figures in their notes (1,591 vs 1,668)**, so they were built from two genuinely distinct source rows, and **`archaic gear` / `archaic gears` both exist in this same family**, which is rule 105's warning in its natural habitat. One of the three sources is wrong and this page cannot say which. **Each record was instead aligned to the page row it obviously belongs to** — the singular takes **142-145**, the plural keeps 146-147 — so the file now matches the page exactly either way the merge question is eventually settled.

## !!!! RULE 138 IS CLOSED — the last seven abjuration rows, resolved structurally

Rev 288 derived 13 of the 24 abjuration prefixes and left four families genuinely ambiguous because the DB contains BOTH candidate forms: Cronian `C.`|`Cr.`, Cyllenian `C.`|`Cy.`, Shinryu `S.`|`Sh.`, Triton `T.`|`Tr.`. **The ambiguity dissolves once you ask why the two-letter form exists at all.**

**THE RULE: the DB abbreviates an abjuration family to its own FIRST TWO LETTERS when that two-letter prefix is in the item list, and to the BARE FIRST LETTER otherwise. It never assigns both forms to one family** (each of the 26 prefixes is a distinct five-slot set: 24 families × 5 + slotless `Obl.`/`Lib.` = 122).

**Verified 13 for 13 on the known map.** Aquarian, Dryadic, Earthen, Martial, Neptunal and Wyrmal all begin with two-letter strings — Aq., Dr., Ea., Ma., Ne., Wy. — and **not one of those exists in the item list**, so they take A./D./E./M./N./W. Abyssal and Arean *do* have Ab./Ar. and take them, with A. going to Aquarian. Bushin/Grove/Jovian/Vale/Venerian have their two-letter form and no bare competitor at all.

So: **Cronian → `Cr.` · Cyllenian → `Cy.` · Shinryu → `Sh.` · Triton → `Tr.`**, with the bare `C.`, `S.` and `T.` sets belonging to three of the seven families we have still never met. **All seven rewrites verified present in ffxi_items.json and applied** — `bia`, `khun`, `ma` ×2, `naphula` ×3. **Invalid drops 366 → 359.** Corroboration from the same records: each already stored `Gr.` / `Va.` / `Ve.` correctly beside its unconverted rows.

- **AND THIS PAGE PUBLISHES ABJURATIONS IN DB FORM, WHICH THE WIKI NEVER DOES.** `Dimgruzub`'s Voidwatch drop list prints `F.Abjuration: Lg.`, `C.Abjuration: Hn.` and `T.Abjuration: Hn.` — abbreviated, not spelled out. All three resolve. **First sighting of three of the seven unnamed families, and the first time the wiki has handed us the DB's own spelling.** It does not name them, so they stay unnamed.

Ingot` zero times**, and the same split runs through Sheet (17/0) and Chain (11/0).

- **!!!! 36 STORED DROPS ACROSS 13 MOBS WERE WRONG, AND THE DB'S FORMAT IS UNGUESSABLE.** Every abjuration in the item DB is `<Prefix>.Abjuration: <Slot>` — **with NO SPACE after the prefix dot** — and the slot is abbreviated `Bd. / Ft. / Hd. / Hn. / Lg.`. 122 entries: 24 families × 5 slots, plus the slotless `Lib. Abjuration` and `Obl. Abjuration`. **Fafnir and Nidhogg already stored the correct form (`A.Abjuration: Ft.`), which is what put the class on the radar at all.**

- **THE FAMILY→PREFIX MAP WAS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED.** Candidate prefixes are those that really prefix the family word; then constraint propagation (a family with one candidate claims it, freeing the ambiguous ones); then **every rewritten name is checked against ffxi_items.json before it is written** — the script cannot invent a name. Resolved: **Aquarian→A. · Abyssal→Ab. · Arean→Ar. · Bushin→Bu. · Dryadic→D. · Earthen→E. · Grove→Gr. · Jovian→Jo. · Martial→M. · Neptunal→N. · Vale→Va. · Venerian→Ve. · Wyrmal→W.**

Coordinates untouched; the `Home Point #N (label)` form follows Norg's existing precedent.

## Collapse on leave — every page, not just Omen/Odyssey

- **THE PROBLEM: rev 243 solved this for 71 sections by passing `persist = false`, but the other 43 call sites still used `rememberSaveable`,** and the root `AuctionApp` keeps a `rememberSaveableStateHolder` **per page key** — which is precisely what makes an expanded panel still be expanded when you come back.
- **THE FIX — a PAGE VISIT id.** New top-level `pageVisitCounter` + `LocalPageVisit` CompositionLocal, and a small `SaveableStateHolder.Page(key, epochKey)` wrapper that mints a **new visit id every time a page is entered** and provides it down the tree. All **35 page branches** now route through it (`holder.SaveableStateProvider(` → `holder.Page(`). `CollapsibleSection` keys its saved state on `"collapse_${stateKey}_$visit"`. **Scrolling never changes the visit, so a panel you opened stays open while you scroll; leaving and returning mints a new id, so the page opens fully collapsed.**
- **!! DELIBERATELY NOT DONE BY CLEARING THE STATE HOLDER.** `SaveableStateHolder.removeState(key)` would have been one line, but it throws away **everything** saved for that page — including scroll position. Backing out of a mob would then jump the bestiary list back to the top. The visit id resets only the collapse state.
- **The `else -> holder.Page("search", ui.mode)` branch takes an explicit epoch key**, because ONE SaveableStateProvider key (`"search"`) serves every top-level tab; without the extra key, switching tabs would not have counted as leaving a page.
- Import added: `androidx.compose.runtime.saveable.SaveableStateHolder` (the extension's receiver type; only `rememberSaveableStateHolder` was imported before). Brace/paren balance verified against the pre-edit file: **+5/+5 braces, +5/+5 parens**, all from the new helper. **NOT COMPILE-CHECKED** — no Android SDK here.
- **AWAITING COMPILE** (201, 210, 211-263, **278**).

## Coo Keja — the page says 37, and the digit proves it

- The second, sharper Meriphataud shot settles rev 271's open question **without changing anything**: the record's 37 was right and my earlier "57" was a misread.
- **HOW IT WAS PROVEN, and this is the reusable part.** Single 5px digits defeat template matching (rev 271), but they do NOT defeat a **row-by-row bitmap diff against a KNOWN digit in the same column**. Coo Keja's cell and Daggerclaw Dracos's `27` render as near-identical bitmaps — **the right glyph is byte-for-byte the same `7`, and the left glyphs differ in exactly two rows**: Daggerclaw's is `##. / ..# / .#. / #.. / ###` (a textbook 2) and Coo Keja's is `##. / ..# / ##. / ..# / ###` (a textbook 3, middle bar present). **Compare a disputed glyph against a known glyph from the SAME column and font, not against an idealized template.**
- The corroboration held too: `Ajase Beads` is a level 30 item, which brackets a 37 and not a 57. **Rule 110 stands and is now confirmed rather than merely plausible.**

- **NEW STANDING RULE: when a zone page's Genus column names a family and our record has NO `fam`, take the page's.** Swept all **eight** zone rosters processed this session — Eldieme, Jugner, Monastic Cavern, Altar Room, Attohwa Chasm, Castle Oztroja, Garlaige Citadel, Meriphataud Mountains, **277 distinct records** — and exactly **one** still had `fam=None`: **`kaboom`** (Garlaige Citadel, Genus **Bomb**). ## The `(monster)` suffix — why nothing was renamed yet

- **22 records carry `(monster)`, and EVERY ONE OF THEM ALREADY HAS A BARE TWIN IN THE FILE.** So the suffix cannot simply be stripped — each rename is a **collision**, i.e. a merge decision, and merges delete records. Nothing was renamed; here is the whole class, classified, so one ruling closes it:
  - **A — 14 where the bare twin is a fam=None, zone-less STUB and the `(monster)` record is the real mob** (it has the family, the zones, twice the fields): black pudding, bolster, bonfire, brunhilde, cannonball, condor, expunger, grenade, ixtab, lycopodium, ochu, **odontotyrannus**, tyrfing, wildfire. **Fold the stub's fields in, delete the stub, rename the survivor to the bare name.**
  - **B — 5 where BOTH records are substantive** and need a per-case look: antares, chigoe, chigre, crawler, gnole.
  - **C — 2 where it is the other way round**, the bare record is real and the `(monster)` one is the near-empty stub: gessho, pixie. **Delete the `(monster)` stub.**
  - **D — 1 genuinely different pair: `siren` is fam=**Avatar** and `siren (monster)` is fam=**Lesser Bird**.** Two different creatures sharing a name — this one is NOT a duplicate and needs a real disambiguator, not a merge.
  - **`brunhilde` and `siren` are TRIPLES** — bare + `(monster)` + `(nm)`.
- **WHY THE SUFFIX EXISTS AT ALL: the wiki appends "(Monster)" when an ITEM shares the name.** This zone proves it — the NM row reads `Odontotyrannus (Monster)` and its own drop is the `Odontotyrannus` weapon. Bonfire, Grenade, Cannonball, Tyrfing, Condor, Expunger, Bolster, Antares and Wildfire are all FFXI items too. **It is a wiki page-title artifact, never part of the in-game name — which is exactly the user's rule.**
- **`(nm)` is the file's own convention and is untouched by this** (`bloodsucker (nm)`, `alexander (nm)`, …).

**Rev 262 — 2026-07-25. UI: every top-level heading in every tab now uses ONE colour, and a horizontal swipe on the body walks the top menu. USER: "can we color all top menu entries across each tab the same color? And can we swipe left and right to change tab from top menus?"** KOTLIN only — no data touched. 58 changed lines in `AuctionApp.kt`, 4 new lines in `theme/Color.kt`.

- **HEADER TIERS ARE NOW NAMED, NOT SCATTERED.** Three new palette entries in `Color.kt`: **`HeaderL1` (gold, = AccentGold), `HeaderL2` (blue, = JobsBlue), `HeaderL3` (0xFF7E8AA0)**. Every top-level heading in every tab is `HeaderL1`. Changing the app's heading colour is now a one-line edit in one file.
- **What was actually inconsistent.** `GroupHeader` — the top entry on Bestiary, Zones and Items — was **AccentRed**, while `CollapsibleSection` (the top entry on Content, Jobs, Hobbies, Events) defaulted to **JobsBlue**, and four call sites hand-passed **AccentGold** on top of that. Three different colours for the same rung. All three are now `HeaderL1`, and **the four hand-passed overrides were deleted** so nothing can drift apart again.
- `SubGroupHeader` moved AccentGold → **`HeaderL2`** and `SubSubHeader` moved a hardcoded orange **`Color(0xFFE8912D)`** — a value that was not in the palette at all — → **`HeaderL3`**, so the bestiary's three-deep tree still reads as a descending ramp underneath the now-gold top rung. The `($subCount)` badge went JobsBlue → TextMuted since JobsBlue is L2's colour now.
- **SWIPE TO CHANGE TAB.** The eight modes were an inline `listOf(...)` inside the pill row; they are now a single top-level **`MODES`** list that both the pill row and the swipe gesture read, so **the gesture and the menu can never disagree about what comes next**. A `detectHorizontalDragGestures` on the body Column steps one mode per swipe past a **72.dp** threshold.
- **Two deliberate calls on the gesture.** (1) **Clamped, not wrapped** — swiping right on Items or left on Hobbies does nothing rather than teleporting across the app. (2) **The pill row keeps its own scroll**, so dragging on the pills still just scrolls the pills; only drags on the body change tab. The detector sits on the parent Column and the pill row's `horizontalScroll` claims the gesture first, which is what makes that work.
- **The selected pill now scrolls itself into view** on every mode change. Eight pills do not fit on a phone, so without this a swipe could land you on a tab whose own pill was off-screen. Keyed on `tabScroll.maxValue` as well as the mode so it still fires on the first layout pass.
- **NOT COMPILE-CHECKED HERE** (no Android SDK in this environment), but the edit is brace-balanced against the original — +7/+7 braces, +11/+11 parens — and every symbol used (`LaunchedEffect`, `rememberScrollState`, `pointerInput`, `detectHorizontalDragGestures`) was already imported. `HeaderL1/2/3` resolve through the existing `ui.theme.*` wildcard import.
- **If the flat gold reads wrong anywhere**, the likely spot is a `CollapsibleSection` nested inside another one (Odyssey's Sheol A/B/C → Notorious Monsters, Sortie's sections): those now match their parent. Passing `titleColor = HeaderL2` at those call sites is a one-line fix each.
- **AWAITING COMPILE** (201, 210, 211-262). Uleguerand is still the one zone left in the Abyssea sweep.

## Shinryu

- **!! `Protostar` HAD THE WRONG SUBJECT — the worst ability error found in this project.** The def read "resets the timers of all *its* unused abilities", i.e. a self-buff. The page says it **resets every ready job ability on its TARGETS to full recast**. That is a whole-party ability wipe at 33% HP and it is the single most important thing to know about the move; the file was telling you to ignore it.
- **!! `Mighty Guard` was wrong twice, which is what you spotted.** It is not just Regain. It restores ~15% of Shinryu's HP **and** raises **two separate buffs**: a **one-minute damage shield** and the Regain. The shield **nullifies spell damage and standard melee outright** — weapon skills and the occasional crit punch through — and **the Regain can be dispelled but the shield cannot**. The file also had the Regain at **100 TP/tick; the page says 10**. The old "nullifies any damage under 300" clause is not what the page describes and was dropped — **if that 300 figure came from somewhere you trust, say so and it goes back as a second line.**
- **HP GATES WERE WRONG.** The old note said Supernova and Protostar arrive "below 50%". They arrive at **33%**, and **66%** is its own gate bringing **Atomic Ray, Dark Matter, tier-2 Ancient Magic and tier-5 -ga**. Both gates are now on the mob and on each ability's own note.
- **TWO NEW ABILITIES DEFINED: `HP Cloak` and `Battle Stances`**, both typed `Special`. The stance mechanic was buried in a note; it is a mechanic you play around, so it now sits in the ability list where you will actually see it.
- **The Comet/Meteor stance claim was softened.** The old note asserted "spread → Meteor, down → Comet" as fact. The page marks it **likely but unconfirmed**, and the note now says so.
- Seven more defs rewritten with what was missing: Draw-In (players who have taken no action are not drawn in; it also draws at random into TP moves), Cataclysmic Vortex (Shell and -MDT% cut it; the enmity reset usually pulls a Draw-In that interrupts your cures), Cosmic Breath (fires even with nobody in range), Gyre Charge and Dark Matter (damage types), Atomic Ray and Supernova (HP gates, Doom clears on exit).
- **Notes went from 2 lines to 12** and now carry: melee swings count as TP moves so "!!" must be timed into the gaps; the swings are a ~10-yalm cone blocked by 1-4 shadows; the **tail hits with Additional Effect: Stun**, which is why retreating after a Draw-In is dangerous; **stagger windows key off time ENGAGED, not time entered**; immune to Stun but open to Slow/Paralyze/Addle/Blind; **Atma is granted on exiting as well as winning** if a red weakness was triggered; the two Primeval Brew traps (Supernova's Doom needs a Doom Screen, and brewing into spread wings feeds it a huge heal); the 30-minute clock; and that **it is not a dragon-family monster** despite the name.
- **Shinryu also took the Zone Boss role for Abyssea-Empyreal Paradox** — it was the last flat Abyssea tag in the file, and it is the entire zone.

For peculiar foes, it should be peculiar foes > zone > all mobs listed, no families. Let's add Unity Mobs next. Unity Mobs > all mobs listed in order of level."**

- **`contentNested` now picks a layout per tag** rather than always nesting by family:
  - **`Peculiar Foes` → Content > ZONE > mobs.** Zones alphabetical, mobs by name inside, **no family level**. Each of the 17 has one zone, so it reads as 15 zone headers (Xarcabard holds the three of objective XV). **Rows under a zone header pass `inZone`**, so a mob shows that zone's band the way the Zone view does.
  - **`Unity Mobs` → Content > mobs by LEVEL, no sub-header at all.** Sorted `levelLo`, then `levelHi`, then name. **The layout is in place and waiting for the tags** — no mob carries `Unity Mobs` yet, so the group won't appear until the screenshots land.
  - **anything else → Content > FAMILY > mobs**, the original shape, so a new tag renders sensibly before it gets its own rule.
- **Mechanism**: a sub-group key of `""` means *flat* — the renderer emits rows straight under the content header with no `SubGroupHeader`. That keeps one code path for both shapes instead of branching the whole LazyColumn.
- **Header count is now `distinctBy { it.key }`** rather than a sum of bucket sizes: under the zone layout a mob with two zones would otherwise be counted twice.
- Row keys stay unique per layout — `"$ctn|$sub|${it.key}"` grouped, `"$ctn||${it.key}"` flat.

That is rule 3's copy-from-a-neighbour shape, but the neighbour is three rows away — what identifies it is not adjacency but **the arithmetic the block obeys**. Rule 66 says suspicious regularity in a MISS list is evidence of a lookup bug; this is the mirror image — **regularity in the DATA is what makes a single wrong value visible**, so when a page publishes a stepped block, check the whole block against the step before writing any of it.

### The Content view — 3 files, AWAITING COMPILE

- **`MobDb.kt`**: `Mob` gains **`val content: List<String> = emptyList()`** (appended last, defaulted, and the ctor call is all NAMED arguments so nothing else moves) + `content = strList(o, "content")` in `load`. **A LIST, NOT A STRING, ON PURPOSE**: `strList` is `optJSONArray(k) ?: emptyList()`, which is null-safe, whereas an `optString` field hands back the literal `"null"` for a JSON null — the rev-127 null-poison class. A mob can also sit in more than one content.

**53. !! A zoneinfo ROW'S `n` IS NOT A LABEL — IT IS THE PRIMARY KEY OF THE NAVIGATION.** `selectMobByName` lowercases it and does an exact `mobDb.get`. **So a zoneinfo name is simultaneously (a) what the user reads, (b) what the tap resolves, and (c) unvalidated by anything.** Two rows sharing a name is not cosmetic duplication — it is two rows wired to one record. **Write the record's own `n` into the zoneinfo row, always, and never a prettier short form.**

**Rev 154 — 2026-07-23. PER-ZONE LEVELS ARE INDEPENDENT — the schema already said so, the NAVIGATION didn't. 3 Kotlin edits across 2 files. USER: "if one zone has a mob as 2-4 level and another has 3-5, they are independent of each other... we need the app to reflect that"**

- **NO SCHEMA CHANGE WAS NEEDED — mobs.json and the model already store one level PER ZONE.** `Mob.zones` is `List<Pair<String, String?>>` (MobDb.kt:32) and **`MobZoneRow` (AuctionApp.kt:919) already renders each zone with its own level in gold**: `Ghelsba Outpost — Lv 3-6` / `Fort Ghelsba — Lv 8-10`. The per-zone truth was there; it just wasn't reaching the header.
- **!! THE BUG WAS IN THE TAP.** `MobRow` under a zone header deliberately shows **that zone's** level in its subtitle (AuctionApp.kt:236-241, with a comment saying exactly that) — but the row's `clickable` called **`vm.selectMob(mob)`, which never set `mobLevelCtx`**. So the list row read **Lv 3-6**, you tapped it, and the detail header read **Lv 3–10**. `selectMobByName(name, level)` (used by the zoneinfo NM/mob rows at 1185/1199) always passed the level; `selectMob` was the one path that dropped it. **Fixed: `MobRow` now passes `inZone` through.**
- **!! SECOND, QUIETER BUG — `selectMob` never RESET `mobLevelCtx` either.** Only `clearMob()` and `back()` did, so a per-zone level from a previously-viewed mob could persist onto a *different* mob's header. **The new `selectMob(mob, inZone = null)` resolves the level from `mob.zones` and writes `""` when there is no zone — so it now clears as well as sets.** One call site file-wide (AuctionApp.kt:228), and the parameter is defaulted, so nothing else changes.
- **THE HEADER'S REMAINING HONESTY GAP IS NOW LABELLED.** Arriving from the Family view or search there IS no zone context, so the header can only show the global `lv` band — and that band is a **summary across independent ranges**, not a range. Added a muted **"varies by zone — see Zones"** subline, shown only when `mobLevelCtx` is empty AND the mob has more than one distinct per-zone level. cheiroptera stops reading as a continuous Lv 3–10.
- **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY *NOT* CHANGED.** `lv` stays as the global band — search, sort and the family/type lists all use it, and it is the right field for "roughly what level is this thing". **The zone pass's rules do NOT assume zones agree**: rule 3 is a *detector* that only fires when the PAGE publishes a different value, so it can never collapse two legitimately-different zones into agreement. **rev 153's cheiroptera is the proof — 3-6 and 8-10 were both kept, independent, and `lv` [3,10] is now exactly their union.**

**51. THE PER-ZONE LEVEL IS THE AUTHORITY; `lv` IS A DERIVED SUMMARY, AND NO UI PATH MAY PRESENT THE SUMMARY AS IF IT WERE A RANGE.** A mob at 2-4 in one zone and 3-5 in another has two independent facts and one derived band [2,5] — which is a level it may never actually be in either zone. **Every screen that can know the zone must show the per-zone value; every screen that cannot must say so.** This is also why rule 49's shape is a bug at all (a global band written into a per-zone slot) and why the (kz) class matters (a global band no zone supports).

**52. A LIST ROW AND THE DETAIL SCREEN IT OPENS MUST AGREE — CHECK THE NAVIGATION CALL, NOT JUST THE TWO RENDERERS.** Both renderers here were individually correct and had been for a long time; the defect lived in the one-line `clickable` between them, which silently dropped the context the row had just used. **When two views disagree, diff what the tap PASSES before diffing what each view draws.**

- **!! COMPILE RISK IS NOW 3 FILES, NOT 1.** I cannot compile in this environment. `ZoneInfoDb.kt` + `AuctionApp.kt` have been **awaiting a compile check since rev 131**, and this rev touches **`AuctionApp.kt` again and `AuctionViewModel.kt` for the first time**. All three edits were read back in full context, checked for name collisions (`zoneLvls` was free file-wide; `lvlText` was the only prior binding), and brace/paren balance was compared against the original zip and is **unchanged**. `TextMuted`, `TextSoft` and `mob.zones` were all verified present at the edit sites. **That is not a substitute for a build — please compile before trusting any of it.**

Given that it now holds the authoritative levels, defaulting it open (or opening it only when the mob has >1 zone) is a one-argument change. **Say the word.**

**46. !! zoneinfo's `nms[].lv` IS A MIRROR OF `nmlv`, NOT AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE — it matches the record's own `nmlv` in 844 of 877 cases (96%).** An (lo) cross-check row sourced from `nms[]` is therefore usually **mobs.json arguing with itself**, not two intakes disagreeing. **zoneinfo's `mobs[]` (the Adversaries lists) IS a genuine second intake** — it has no counterpart field in mobs.json, and every real zone-pass hit came from it (fighting pugil, orcish mesmerizer, enchanted bones). **Never quote an `nms[]` row back as corroboration for an NM level.**

**47. `nmlv` OVERRIDES `lv` IN THE UI, BUT THE ZONE VIEW OVERRIDES `nmlv` — so a level contradiction is VISIBLE, not latent.** `MobDb.levelText` = `nmLevel.isNotEmpty() -> "Lv $nmLevel"`, so **`lv` is never rendered on a record carrying `nmlv`**; but `AuctionApp.kt:569` = `if (mobLevelCtx.isNotEmpty()) "Lv $ctx" else mob.levelText`, and `AuctionViewModel.selectMobByName(name, level)` fills `mobLevelCtx` from the zone entry. **Be'Hya Hundredwall was showing Lv 80 from the Family/search view and Lv 30 from the Zone view — same mob, same session.** That is the user-facing symptom of every one of the 34 remaining (ls) cases.

**48. A COMPOUND `nmlv` GENERATES SPURIOUS CROSS-CHECK CONFLICTS.** `emperor arthro` stores `nmlv = "99 (CL 122)"` — base level 99, Content Level 122. mobs.json's zone entry reads **99**, zoneinfo reads **122**, and **both are parsing the same string correctly, just different halves.** `strix` has the identical shape (`"99 (CL 125)"`). **Any parser over `nmlv` must handle the `N (CL M)` form.**

**CORRECTIONS TO REV 151 — that block overstates two things and this one supersedes it:**
- **`emperor arthro` 99 vs 122 was listed as a worst-case conflict. It is a FALSE POSITIVE** (rule 48).
- **D3's 162 overstates the independent signal.** Split by source table: **135 come from zoneinfo's `mobs[]`** (real two-source conflicts, worth a screenshot) and **27 from `nms[]` — of which 21 are pure `nmlv` mirrors** (rule 46). **The number actually worth chasing with pages is ~141, not 162.**
- The same caveat narrows **(lq)**: bucket **C (283 level fills)** is still additive and rule-1-safe, but any of its rows that come from `nms[]` are just copying `nmlv` into a zone entry — correct, though not new information. **B (1,998 zone adds) is unaffected and remains the biggest clean win.**

- **(ls) OPEN, MEASURED — the `lv` vs `nmlv` contradiction class.** **929 records carry `nmlv`; 114 have an `nmlv` DISJOINT from their own `lv` band** — thu'ban 135 vs [99,99], grand grenade 128 vs [99,99], goblin preceptor 80 vs [45,49], the Dynamis statue block (~80 vs [65,70]), the five Qiqirn NMs (~80 vs [90,92]). **34 have a stored zone level disjoint from `nmlv`** — that subset is exactly what rule 47 makes visible to a user. **NOT all 114 are bugs**: many are an approximate `~80` sitting against a measured band, which may be deliberate. **be'hya resolved in favour of `lv`, i.e. `nmlv` was the liar — but ONE case is not a pattern, so nothing was generalized.** **Needs a policy call: does `nmlv` win, does `lv`, or must `lv` always contain `nmlv`?** An audit.py section would stop it growing.

- **ELEMENTAL eco (rev 98) — three families this pass; the category has 67 pages, so MORE Elemental families follow (Umbril = 18 recs is its own family; Yanthu, Pixie, Magic Sludge, Polevik, etc. later).**
  - **ELEMENTAL (64, Black Mage, crys Varies) = a 12-TABLE SWIPE family — the biggest swipe set yet.** 8 pure element grids + 4 hybrid grids (Baelfyr=Fire+Light, Gefyrst=Ice+Water, Ungeweder=Wind+Lightning, Byrgen=Earth+Dark). `family_resist_sets["Elemental"]` order = [Fire,Ice,Wind,Earth,Thunder,Water,Light,Dark,Baelfyr,Gefyrst,Ungeweder,Byrgen]. **Convention (WIKI-authoritative, replacing the old -25/+25 import):** the 5 weapon-skill types (Slashing/Blunt/H2H/Piercing/Ranged) all **-75%** (=25%; Physical/Magical/Breath land full); a pure elemental **-95%** (=5%) on its own element + the one it beats on the wheel, **+50%** (=150%) on its weakness (Wind is the 2-weak Ice+Water; Light/Dark st only their own element); a hybrid **-95** on its 2 primaries, **-15** (=85%) on the other 4, **+50** on its 2 weaknesses.
    - **THE OLD PER-MEMBER DATA WAS CORRUPT** — base Baelfyr was stamped both weak-to-Fire AND resists-Fire (impossible). So all 63 mappable members were RE-STAMPED to their element's set (each opens on its element, swipes the rest). Mapping: name-keyword → hybrid; element-Yanthu by name (scorched→Baelfyr, glaciated→Gefyrst, electrified→Ungeweder, entombed→Byrgen); else pure by **weakness→own-element** (the wheel: Water→Fire, Fire→Ice, Ice→Wind, Wind→Earth, Earth→Thunder, Lightning→Water, Dark→Light, Light→Dark), name fallback for hollow/apex stubs. Only **Staumarth** (Thunder-weather hybrid, no published table) kept its own cleaned grid. Merged the 2 `fam=Elementals` typo records in. Created 6 hybrid ability defs + enriched Entomb/Tenebral Crush; stamped hybrid TP moves on baelfyr/gefyrst/ungeweder/byrgen members EXCEPT ascended (Ru'Aun) & apex (Abyssea) — the page says those versions "do not use TP moves."
    - **BUG (found + fixed): a None-magnitude junk element inside a member's `wk` misclassified the mapping** — water elemental's `[Lightning +25, Wind None]` matched 'Wind' before 'Lightning' and sent it to the Earth set. Fix: only real-magnitude (`e[1]` truthy) weaknesses drive the wheel mapping; required a pristine re-run.
  - **HEARTWING (7, White Mage, crys Light) = SINGLE table, NO swipe** (NOT in family_resist_sets). Light elementals casting Dia/Cure/Regen/Protect/Shell/Banish/Holy (20 MDB). Grid: Light & Dark both **-95%** (=5%), every other element **-50%**, Magical & Breath **-50%**, and **WEAK to Piercing & Ranged +100% (=200%)** — the first family stamped with a physical-type WEAKNESS. 4 new abilities (Heartfelt Aura / Impairing Glister / Ancestral Banishment / Crippling Gleam).
  - **MONOCEROS (12, Warrior, Fire Crystal) = a 2-TABLE SWIPE-BY-NAME family** (the unicorns). USER: "unicorns are base on names for resist." `family_resist_sets["Monoceros"]` = [Monocero, Alicorn]. **Monocero** (Ixion form): Lightning -70, Dark -50, Fire/Wind/Ice/Water -30, wk Earth +30. **Alicorn** (white form): Light -70, Fire/Wind/Lightning -40, Ice/Earth/Water -15, wk Dark +30. Mapping by NAME: `*alicorn` + peirithoos → Alicorn; `*ixion` + base → Monocero. Added `auroral alicorn` (was fam=None) into the family. det [Magic,Sound]. Form-gated kit: shared Acheron Kick / Damsel Memento / Rampant Stance + Monocero-only Wrath of Zeus / Lightning Spear (thunder) + Alicorn-only Grace of Hera / Scintillant Lance (light) — 7 new defs. Trait Movement Speed +75% passive / +250% aggressive. NM zones + validated drops (Dark Ixion, Karkadann, Indrik, Veiled Ixion/Alicorn, Peirithoos, Oryx).

- **KEY NEW LESSONS.** (1) **When the existing per-member resist data is self-contradictory, re-stamp the whole family from the wiki tables** rather than trusting the import — the Elemental hybrids proved the old -25/+25 stamps were both wrong-magnitude and internally inconsistent. (2) **A None-magnitude junk entry inside `wk`/`st` can silently drive a name/element mapping the wrong way** — filter on truthy magnitude before using wk to infer an element. (3) **A family can WEAKEN to a physical damage type** (Heartwing Piercing/Ranged +100) — `wk` is not elements-only. (4) **SWIPE-BY-NAME** (Monoceros) generalizes the swipe beyond Cores: a member opens on the table whose name keyword it matches.

**Rev 96 — 2026-07-21. EMPTY ecosystem COMPLETE — the "Core" resist-swipe families. This block catches the handoff up from rev 92 through all seven Empty families built across revs 93–96: Craver, Gorger, Receptacle, Seether, Thinker, Weeper, Wanderer. The swipeable Core resist grid was RE-ENABLED for these (first active `family_resist_sets` since Peiste). `family_resist_sets` keys now = [Craver, Gorger, Seether, Thinker, Weeper, Wanderer] (Receptacle is not a Core family).**
Author: BalladOfWorms.

- **THE EMPTY "CORE" MECHANIC + THE SWIPE.** Empty-type mobs (the Promyvion / Spire / Escha "spawned from a person's emotions" enemies) have an elemental **Core** that fixes their resistances. Each family's category page publishes **8 full "&lt;Elem&gt; Core Resistances" grids** — one per Core alignment — stored as `family_resist_sets["&lt;Family&gt;"]` = a list of 8 `{label, wk, st}` sets. In the app these render as a **swipeable resist grid** (swipe through the 8 Cores). A standard Empty mob carries NO own `wk`/`st`, so its grid opens on the first Core (Fire) and swipes.
  - **THE 8-SET TABLE IS SHARED — but NOT perfectly rigid.** Craver = Gorger = Seether = Thinker = **Weeper**, byte-for-byte (each is a verified `deepcopy(==)` of Craver's). **Wanderer is the exception:** its Wind Core is weak to **Ice only** (not Ice + Water — Water reads 100% on its Wind grid), so `family_resist_sets["Wanderer"] != Craver`. **Lesson: always pixel-check the Wind grid; don't assume a deepcopy.** Pattern (element order = the locked Fire/Wind/Lightning/Light/Ice/Earth/Water/Dark): each Core resists **its own element + the one it beats on the wheel at 5%** (stored `st = -95%`) and is **weak 150%** (stored `wk = +50%`) **to what beats it**. Fire{st Fire,Ice / wk Water}; Ice{st Ice,Wind / wk Fire}; **Wind{st Wind,Earth / wk Ice,Water}** (the lone 2-weak outlier); Earth{st Earth,Lightning / wk Wind}; Thunder{st Lightning,Water / wk Earth}; Water{st Water,Fire / wk Lightning}; Light{st Light / wk Dark}; Dark{st Dark / wk Light}. **The Thunder Core's element STRING is `Lightning`** (label reads "Thunder Core"; ELEM_ORDER has no "Thunder").
  - **THE KOTLIN GUARD (added rev 93, `AuctionApp.kt` ~line 587, unchanged since).** The swipe is family-generic: `val resistSets = vm.resistSets(mob.family)` (looks up `familyResistSetsMap[family]` in `MobDb.kt`), then `ownGridMatchesASet = resistSets.any { it.weaknesses == mob.weaknesses && it.strengths == mob.strengths }`, and `if (resistSets.isNotEmpty() && (!hasMods || ownGridMatchesASet)) SwipeableResistGrid(...) else if (hasMods) ResistGrid(...)`. So a member with its OWN distinct fixed grid that matches no Core set (the "Glassy &lt;Family&gt;" NMs) renders its own `ResistGrid` instead of the swipe. **No Kotlin change was needed for Gorger/Seether/Thinker** — writing the guard generic in rev 93 was the payoff.

- **CRAVER (rev 93) — 12 records, 1st Empty family.** `family_eco["Craver"]="Empty"`. **det [Sight,Sound,Scent]** (3-icon box), **crys Varies**. Base kit Brain Spike / Empty Thrash / Material Fend / Murk / Promyvion Brume; NM-only Carousel / Impalement / View Sync. Created 3 defs (Carousel, Empty Thrash, View Sync); Murk el=Wind. **Glassy Craver** (Geas Fete/Omen) has a full own grid (all-8 elems -40 / Piercing +50) → own ResistGrid via the guard. Warder of Mercy (Escha RuAun), Coveter (Promyvion-Mea) enriched. Usurper is a Craver (Abyssea-Tahrongi), enriched rev 94.

- **GORGER (rev 94) — 19 records, 2nd Empty family, Warrior / Red Mage.** `family_resist_sets["Gorger"]` = deepcopy of Craver (asserted `==`). **det [Sight,Sound,Scent]**, **crys Varies**, job Warrior. Base kit Promyvion Barrier / Quadratic Continuum / Spirit Absorption / Stygian Flatus / Vanity Drive; NM-only Blessing Sync + Fission. Created 5 defs; Stygian Flatus el=Ice; fixed "Vanity Dive"→"Vanity Drive". **Glassy Gorger** own grid = wk Slashing +50% ONLY (rest "?") → own ResistGrid. Depths Digester / Satiator / Warder of Loyalty (Escha RuAun) enriched. `faygorger ram`/`sheep` are Sheep/Ram-type, NOT Gorger.

- **RECEPTACLE (rev 95) — 6 records, NOT a Core family.** `family_eco["Receptacle"]="Empty"`. The category "Receptacle Resistances" grid is entirely **"?" (unknown)** — a single grid, not the 8-Core wheel — so **NO `family_resist_sets`** was created. Stationary Memory Receptacle portal-objects (destroy the correct one to open the next Promyvion level). **det ['Sound']** (lone red speaker; stripped bad ['Scent'] import), **crys None** (box shows "N" = no crystal, it's an object), job None. Kit = **['Empty Seed']** (new def: AoE 20' physical + Knockback) on all 6. **Memory Receptacle keeps its existing per-mob grid** (wk all-4-physical +100% / st all-8-elements -50% — plausible object profile, not wiki-confirmed → open ie); nm, lv[30,50], zones Promyvion-Dem/Mea/Holla/Vahzl + portal note. Colored Blue/Green/Red/Yellow → Spire of Vahzl (Pulling the Plug). Recollector: stripped junk `wk=['Piercing Damage',None]`.

Members: Seether (std, Promyvion-Holla/Dem/Mea 31-38 + -Vahzl 51-58 + Spire of Mea), Provoker (NM, Promyvion-Vahzl, forced spawn via Satiator Remnant at ???/E-7 5th level; drops Recollection of Anxiety + White Memosphere), Meditator (NM ~80, Abyssea-La Theine; 10 Pearlescent light; Colorful demilune abyssite upgrade), Apex Livid Rager (high-tier, all 4 Promyvion). **"Stray"** (39-51 Promyvion-Vahzl) is in the Adversaries table but not Category:Seether → skipped here; **rev 96 confirmed it is a Wanderer member** (it also appears in Weeper's adversary table). Open (ig) closed.

- **THINKER (rev 95) — 12 records, Core family.** `family_resist_sets["Thinker"]` = deepcopy of Craver (Fire/Ice/Wind + Water/Light/Dark read to confirm; Earth/Thunder implied by the rigid wheel). **det [Sight,Sound,Scent]**, **crys Varies**, job Warrior. **Big kit:** base 11 = Binary/Spirit/Trinary Absorption + Binary/Spirit/Trinary Tap + Empty Cutter / Negative Whirl / Pain Sync / Stygian Vapor / Winds of Promyvion; **Shadow Spread NM-only** (base+SS = 12 on the 6 NMs). Created 6 defs (Binary Absorption, Binary Tap, Pain Sync, Spirit Tap, Trinary Absorption, Winds of Promyvion); enriched Empty Cutter (crit); softened Trinary Tap note; **left Spirit Absorption unchanged** (shared with Gorger). **Glassy Thinker** (Reisenjima Henge mini-boss) own grid = wk Slashing +50% ONLY → own ResistGrid; kept its 7-move kit; drops Adad Amulet / Knobkierrie / Adapa Shield. NMs: Brooder (Abyssea-La Theine ~85; Serpentes Sabots / Libeccio Mantle), Cerebrator (Promyvion-Holla lv38; Cerebrator Remnant / Teal Memosphere KIs), Warder of Dignity (Escha RuAun; casts Fire/Blizzard/Aero VI → `sp`; Impassive Mantle / Thereoid Greaves / Henic Torque / Eschalixir), Ruminator / Ponderer / Agonizer. Event mobs zoned (Cogitator/Wreaker→Spire of Holla; Agonizer/Contemplator→Spire of Vahzl; Ponderer→Promyvion-Vahzl).

- **WEEPER (rev 96) — Core family, swipe = deepcopy of Craver** (all 8 grids pixel-verified `==`; Wind is the normal 2-weak Ice+Water). **det [Sight,Sound,Scent]**, **crys Varies**, job Warrior. Kit = Auroral Drape / Empty Cutter / Vacuous Osculation / Hexagon Belt, **plus the element-locked "Memory of &lt;element&gt;" nukes** (8, one per Core — kept to family_notes only, NOT stamped per-mob, since each Weeper uses only its own Core's nuke). Notes: innate -10% Def penalty + Magic Defense Bonus trait (aspirable; +10/+12/+14 MDB by zone tier). Members: weeper (std, Promyvion 25-57 + Spire of Holla), Apex Woeful Lamenter, Wailer (NM, Promyvion-Vahzl trade-pop via Coveter Remnant), Lachrymater (Abyssea-Tahrongi NM — drag onto the G-10 point to spawn Myrmecoleon), Lamenter (Monster — drops the Moaning Vestige, Lachrymater's pop item).

- **WANDERER (rev 96) — Core family, swipe = Craver's sets EXCEPT the Wind Core (weak Ice only).** The first Empty family whose Core table deviates. **det [Sight,True Sight,Sound,Scent]** (4-icon box — one more than the 3-icon Weeper/Gorger; the extra leading circular glyph = True Sight), **crys Varies**, **NO job** (family box has no Typical Job). Kit = Aura of Persistance / Empty Beleaguer / Mirage / **Vanity Dive**. Notes: MP + Magic Defense Bonus; innate Evasion Bonus + -10% Def penalty (Apex Idle Drifters ~+40 evasion). Members: wanderer (std, Promyvion 22-56 + Spire of Dem), **stray** (Wanderer regular — closes open ig), Apex Idle Drifter, Deviator (NM, Promyvion-Vahzl trade-pop via Cerebrator Remnant), Meanderer (Abyssea-Konschtat, Veridical Conflux #04). **"Vanity Dive" (Wanderer, single-target) ≠ "Vanity Drive" (Gorger, conal)** — two distinct abilities, confirming the rev-94 Glassy-Gorger typo fix.

- **VERIFY-BY-VIEW lesson (Core grids).** The red/green pct-cell classifier over-reports "st": 100% cells pick up 7–13 stray red pixels from antialiasing/bleed. The GREEN (weak) reads are clean; the definitive check is **cropping each element-value row and reading it directly**. Header bars are (76,78,80) grey but the grid spans only the right ~30% of image width, so detect headers within the grid sub-region and anchor columns on the element-gem centroids.

**Rev 58 — 2026-07-20. SUB-TYPES RETIRED — flattened into their families (data-only, no Kotlin).**
Author: BalladOfWorms.
- **USER: "remove the sub type listing, though keeping mobs correct resist, abilities, notes, etc... I pull
  up crawlers now, I get crawlers and eruca. I want to see them all as crawlers but the individual keeps the
  correct info and image if it's eruca."** So: flatten every sub-type into its family for the LISTING, but
  each mob stays self-contained (own grid/kit/notes/image).
- **Pure DATA change — no Kotlin edits.** The mob-browser already flattens on its own: list code is
  `subGroups = typeMobs.groupBy { it.sub ?: type }` then `if (subGroups.size <= 1) items(typeMobs){...}` —
  so once no mob has a `sub`, every family is a single group and lists flat. `SubGroupHeader` only prints
  "($subCount)" when `subCount > 1`, so no stray "(1)". `iconForMob` = per-mob `img` FIRST, then sub-type
  image, then family icon — so materialising the sub-type image onto each member preserves the exact icon.
- **Migration**: for every mob with a `sub`, (1) if it had no own `img`, copied its sub-type's `img` down
  (**1,167 imgs materialised**); (2) appended the sub-type's notes to the mob's own notes, deduped (**651
  mobs**); (3) cleared `sub` (**1,337 mobs**). Then **emptied `family_subtypes` (32 → 0)**. Grids were NOT
  touched — every member already carried its own `wk`/`st` (survey: members_no_grid = 0 across all 32
  families), which is why the card grid was always per-mob. Example verified: **Crawler now lists all 63
  flat** — 13 on eruca.png (+ the Eruca note), 47 on crawler.png, 3 green-crawler per-mob overrides
  preserved.
- **2 orphan `fam=None` "Ovim" records** (contumacious/pungent ovim) didn't resolve to the Ram/Ovim
  sub-type (their family was null, so they never got the Ovim image even before) → **folded into `fam="Ram"`
  + Ovim image**; they already had their own grids.
- Dead code left in place (unreachable, no data references it): `SubType`, `subtypes()`, `subtypeNotes()`,
  `SubtypeDetailScreen`, the `iconForMob` sub-type branch. Re-populating `family_subtypes` + `sub` would
  revive it. The old "sub-type = distinct grid/skill" rule is now moot — a distinct grid/model just gets
  per-mob `wk`/`st` + per-mob `img` (the Caturae/Gallu/Demon pattern).
- numbers r58: mobs 6675, abilities 1096, family_eco 124, family_notes 121, **family_subtypes 0** (was 32).
  audit §2 parse THROWS 0 / null 0 / markup 0.

**Rev 39 — 2026-07-17. !!!! THE APP HAS BEEN SHOWING ZERO MOBS SINCE REV 35 AND THIS FIXES IT. !!!!**
Author: BalladOfWorms. **Supersedes rev 38.** USER: *"mobs arent showing at all in app now, either
filter or searched."*

**THE BUG.** `family_subtypes["Skeleton"]` shipped as a **JSON OBJECT** — `{"Skeleton": {"img":
"mobicons/Skeleton.jpg"}, "Draugar": {}}` — where the schema is a **LIST of `{name, wk, st, notes,
img}`** (§3). `MobDb.load` does `so.getJSONArray(f)` over every `family_subtypes` key; org.json's
`getJSONArray` on an object is a **typeMismatch -> JSONException**. And `AuctionViewModel` line 109 is
**`runCatching { MobDb.load(app) }.getOrNull()`** — so the throw is swallowed, **`mobDb` becomes null**,
and every call site is `mobDb?.all() ?: emptyList()` / `mobDb?.search(q) ?: emptyList()`.
**Result: zero mobs, in browse AND filter AND search, with no crash, no toast and nothing in the log.**
The other 30 `family_subtypes` entries were correct; one key bricked the whole feature.

**THE FIX.** Rebuilt as the schema shape. **The grids were not lost** — every member carries its own
`wk`/`st` from the rev-35 stamp and both sets are internally uniform (104 Skeleton records = 1 distinct
grid, 7 Draugar = 1), so the two sub-types were reconstructed from the mobs themselves and cross-check
against the rev-35 notes cell-for-cell: **Skeleton** Impact +25 / H2H +12.5 / Fire +50 / Wind +30 /
Lightning +30 / Light +50 / Earth +30 / Water +30 · Slashing -12.5 / Piercing -50 / Ranged -50 / Dark
-50. **Draugar** the same row 1, then Fire +30 / Wind +15 / Lightning +15 / Light +30 / Earth +15 /
Water +15 · Slashing -12.5 / Piercing -50 / Ranged -50 / **Ice -30** / Dark -50.

**THE GUARD — audit.py §2 now runs a full `MobDb.load` PARSE SIMULATOR and it must read 0.** It
reproduces **every strict org.json call** in load(): `mobs.getJSONObject`, strList's `a.getString(i)`
(im/ab_el/ab/sp/det), modList's `a.getJSONArray(i)` + `e.getString(0)` (wk/st, mobs and subtypes),
notes' `arr.getString(i)`, zones' `e.getString(0)`, `fx`'s getString, `family_icons.getString`,
`family_notes.getJSONArray`, `family_eco.getString`, and **`family_subtypes.getJSONArray`** — the one
that bit. Verified both ways: **0 on the fixed file, and 1 with the bug reintroduced**, naming the key.
**RUN audit.py BEFORE EVERY ZIP.**

Headline lessons:
- **!!!! `runCatching{}.getOrNull()` TURNS A DATA TYPO INTO A SILENT TOTAL OUTAGE. !!!!** This is the
  THIRD time a swallowed exception has hidden a data bug from me — `dhartok`'s bare `img` filename
  (SubtypeImage's `runCatching{}.getOrNull()`, silent placeholder from Plovid to rev 33), the null-poison
  `optString` -> literal `"null"` family header, and now this. **The pattern: whenever the app "just
  shows nothing", look for the swallowed throw FIRST, and check the DATA SHAPE against the Kotlin
  accessor — not the data's meaning.** §4 was "null is poison"; it is really **"the shape must match the
  accessor, and the accessor never tells you when it doesn't."**
- **A GUARD THAT MIRRORS THE PARSER BEATS A GUARD THAT MIRRORS THE SCHEMA.** The schema line in §3
  ("family_subtypes (type->[{name,wk,st,notes,img}])") was **right and stated all along**, and every
  audit run since rev 35 reported "family_subtypes set 31" — a COUNT, which is true of a dict too.
  **Count checks pass through shape bugs. Simulate the reader.**
- **THE DAMAGE WAS ZERO REVS OF DATA BUT FOUR REVS OF USE.** Revs 36-38 (Acrolith / Bomb / Snoll /
  Djinn) all built on a bricked app — the data is fine and none of it needs redoing, but **the user
  could not see any of it.** *(Every family since Skeleton was stamped, delivered and unusable.)*
- **THIS IS WHY §2 SAYS VERIFY THE ZIP.** The session-start check is "pick 3-4 values the family log
  claims and check them" — it checks CONTENT. It would have passed here. **Add: run audit.py on the zip
  you are about to ship and confirm §2 is all zeroes.**

**Skeleton at a glance.** **111 = the category listing's 111 pages, 1:1, no fold and no subtraction
class.** **Earth Crystal — the FIRST Undead family that is not Dark or Ice** / **Sound + Blood** /
**`Black Mage, Thief, Dark Knight, Dragoon`** (four entries in Typical Job, and **no Typical Sub Job row
at all** — the Hound shape). **TWO published grids -> 2 subs, and the USER gave the membership rule:
*"draugur are in the name"*** -> Draugar 7 / Skeleton 104. **`Malediction`'s Condition column reads
*"Draugars only."*** — so the sub qualifies **both** ways (own grid + own kit gate), the Bhoot shape.
**Zones 85/111 — the biggest absolute zone haul in the project**, off a 107-row Adversaries table.

**Vampyr at a glance.** **19 = 19, a clean 1:1.** **Dark Crystal / Sight + Sound + Blood** (2nd family
with the third glyph, after Qutrub) / **`Dark Knight`** (no Typical Sub Job row). **No sub-types.**
`ab` was **EMPTY on all 19** and **all 9 ability names were absent defs — the FIFTH family running.**

Headline findings this rev:
- **!!!! I MIS-ATTRIBUTED A SCREENSHOT FOR A WHOLE REV AND THE RECOVERY IS THE LESSON. !!!!** Rev 34's
  notes recorded image `...764596` as "the Vampyr category page, grid + full ability table". **It is Lord
  Varney's mob page.** The real category page is `...678167`. Nothing was written from the bad
  attribution, but a whole pass was planned on it. **The fix is mechanical, not careful reading: a family
  grid is the ONLY thing on BG with all eight element gems in one horizontal row.** Scanning every
  upload for "how many of the 8 reference gems appear within ±6px of one row" returns 8/8 on exactly the
  category pages and <=6 on every mob page and every listing. **Run that scan on a new batch before
  reading anything — it identifies the category page in one pass and it cannot be fooled by a page that
  merely looks like one.**
- **!!!! A PAGE CAN PRINT AN ELEMENT NEXT TO AN ABILITY NAME AND MEAN SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY. !!!!**
  Vidmapire's General Notes read like a gift: *"Bloodrake: (fire) Fire, en-Plague and Blaze Spikes ·
  Eternal Damnation: (ice) Ice ... · Nosferatu's Kiss: (water) Water ..."* — nine moves, each with an
  element. **It is not the moves' elements.** Vidmapire changes elemental alignment and *"You may
  encourage these TP moves to be used by dealing primarily magical damage of their associated element"* —
  the list is **which element you nuke it with to make it use the move**. The proof is in the pixels:
  its own Type column and the category's agree with each other and **contradict its prose on 3 of the 4
  moves that carry a 2nd icon** — Eternal Damnation is **Dark** (distance 0.0) not Ice, Nosferatu's Kiss
  is **Dark** (0.0) not Water, Nocturnal Servitude is **Light** (0.0) not Dark. Only Wings of Gehenna =
  Wind agrees, by coincidence. **The Corse rule was "an element can hide in the description cell"; this
  is the inverse — prose elements that are not the ability's element. THE TYPE COLUMN IS THE AUTHORITY.**
- **THE BEST-SOURCED ROSE IN THE PROJECT, AND THE FIRST THAT IS NOT "NM ONLY".** Vampyr's category table
  roses `Dirty Breath`, `Minax Glare`, `Nocturnal Servitude` — **167 px of tint inside x 9-236, the name
  cell, with the Condition column completely empty and no blue anywhere.** Five pages then name the
  users, and they do not partition by NM at all: **Wurdalak (`Class: Monster`, a STANDARD mob) publishes
  exactly the six non-rose moves**; **Vidmapire** (Unity NM) publishes the six + Nocturnal Servitude;
  **Lord Asag** *"has access to all Vampyr TP moves **except Dirty Breath**, but including Nocturnal
  Servitude"*; **Sava Savanovic** *"uses the following TP moves"* and lists six including **Dirty Breath
  and Minax Glare but not Nocturnal Servitude**; **Lord Varney** *"**does not use Bloodrake** — so Blue
  Mages cannot learn it from him!"*. Three NMs, three different rose subsets. **Rose means "not the
  standard kit" and nothing more — it never meant NM. Qutrub's `(NM only)` was a fact about Qutrub.**
- **THE UN-ROSED-KIT CORROBORATION IS NOW A PATTERN, NOT A ONE-OFF.** Rev 34 flagged Aynu-kaysey
  publishing exactly the six non-rose Qutrub moves as new evidence. **Wurdalak does the identical thing
  for Vampyr, one family later** — a standard mob's page listing the base kit and nothing else.
  **When a category table roses N rows, look for a plain `Class: Monster` page: its Abilities column is
  the control group.**
- **THE GRID READER IS NOW MECHANICAL, AND IT SCORED 16/16 ON A BLIND CONTROL.** OCR each cell for the
  magnitude + measure the ink colour for the direction (green digits = weak, red = resist, black =
  neutral). Run against the Skeleton grid I had already read by eye: **colour 16/16, magnitude 14/16.**
  The two misses are the *wide* cells — `87.5%` and `112.5%` overflow the 36.6px column and clip to
  `7.5%` / `12.5%`. **Padding the crop is not the fix** (it drags in the neighbour's digits: `5100%1`).
  **Re-OCR a clipped cell alone at psm 8/13** — that is what settled Vampyr's Magical cell, which read
  `13%` at psm 7 and **`75%`** at psm 8 and 13, both agreeing.
- **VAMPYR IS QUTRUB'S MIRROR, AND ITS GRID IS THE MOST LOPSIDED IN THE FILE.** Qutrub takes **+100% from
  all eight damage types**. Vampyr **resists nearly everything**: Magical 75%, Breath 87.5%, all five
  melee types 100%, and elements Fire 85 / Wind 60 / Lightning 85 / Ice 50 / Earth 60 / Water 85 /
  **Dark 5%**. **Its only weakness in all sixteen cells is Light +15%.** Dark 5% ties Vinipata's for the
  lowest cell ever recorded — but this one is a **family** grid, not a single NM's.
- **`vidmapire` lv [99,99] -> [128,128], and the import contradicted itself.** Its Listings box publishes
  Level 128 and **its own `nmlv` already said 128** while `lv` said 99. §8: the mob's page wins.
  **When `lv` and `nmlv` disagree, that is not a judgement call — it is a bug.**
- **TWO IMPORT TYPOS FOUND BY READING THE STAMP OUTPUT: `soaring strigoi` and `soaring vampyr` both
  carried `job: "Dark Kinght"`.** Not an abbreviation, not a variant — a misspelling, on two records, in
  a field with a closed vocabulary. **Print the distinct values of every field you stamp; the junk shows
  up in the list, never in the diff.**

Headline findings this rev:

  ability table (grey header) carries **both**: `Fortifying Wall`'s row is **blue (201,205,224) at 868
  contiguous px = the whole row, every cell** — §5's cursor, exactly in the 600-920 band — while

  (224,206,206) at 228 px, x 28-255 = the Ability column only**, with `Type` / `Area` / `Condition`

  And the blue *also* bleeds 228 px into Fortifying Wall's description row, because the name cell is
  `rowspan=2` — **so the description row of a hovered ability looks exactly like a gate.** Measure the
  MAIN row, not the description row. §5 said blue lives in grey tables and rose in maroon ones; that
  was the *cursor's* palette rule and it still holds — **the GATE is rose in a grey table too.**

  (NM only, first weapon intact)` and `Gen'ei Ryodan (NM only)` — the Corse / Flock Bat / Doomed
  wording again, and again the *generic restriction*, never a content type. **But the new evidence is
  Aynu-kaysey: its own page publishes a six-row ability table that is EXACTLY the six non-rose moves.**
  A mob page independently listing the un-rosed kit and nothing else. Two facts, two pages, one gate.
- **AYNU-KAYSEY'S `Class: Monster` AND ITS SIX-MOVE TABLE AGREE WITH EACH OTHER** — so the `(NM only)`
  gate was applied on the `nm` flag (the Corse *Gala Macabre* precedent) **minus aynu-kaysey**, whose
  own page overrules the family-level gate on both counts. -> Unblest Jambiya + Gen'ei Ryodan on
  `dimgruzub`, `manananggal`, `moshdahn`, `zareehkl the jubilant`; base 6 everywhere else. Its `nm:
  true` was **left as found** — see open (cx).
- **THE THREE `Ambuscade` MOVES ARE DEFINED AND STAMPED ON NOBODY, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** `Phantom

- **THE IMPORT GRID WAS A DIFFERENT DATASET ON A 2x SCALE, AND IT CONTRADICTED ITSELF.** Every Qutrub
  carried `Ice +75%` in `wk` **and** `["Ice", null]` in `st` — weak to Ice *and* resistant to Ice, the
  Boreal Hound (cs) disease. Decoding it: the import is `2 x X` for X = Fire/Light 112.5, Ice 87.5,

- **A SECOND `Fistl. Discharge`: wiki `Zareehkl's Neckpiece` -> DB `Zrkl.'s Neckpiece`.** The DB
  abbreviates **the mob's own name inside its own drop**, and it kills the first four letters, so

  **SEARCH THE OTHER WORD.** (The record already had it right — but only fz proves that.)
