Headline findings this rev:
- **!!!! I STAMPED THE WRONG JOB FORM ON GHOST LAST REV AND HAVE FIXED IT. !!!!** §12's debt table says
  it outright — ***"the file's own answer is the LONG form (`Warrior` 1,803 vs `WAR` 260)"*** — and every
  stamped family agrees: Hecteyes **`Black Mage / Warrior`**, Worm **`Black Mage / Black Mage, Red
  Mage`**, Dullahan **`Paladin / Dark Knight`**, Corse **`Dark Knight, Black Mage`**, Leech / Slug /
  Pugil / Orobon / Doomed **`Warrior`**. **Rev 31 stamped Ghost `BLM / WAR` x75 — the only family in the
  file on the 3-letter form.** Both of my families are now converted (Ghost 79, Hound 39). **This was NOT
  a file-wide sweep** — the other ~1,125 short-form mobs are pre-existing debt and still the user's call.
- **THE APOSTROPHE THING IS REAL BUT `audit.py` ALREADY HANDLES IT — CHECK THE TOOL BEFORE THE HEADLINE.**
  `zones.json` stores **`QuBia Arena`**, **`The Sanctuary of ZiTah`**, **`King Ranperres Tomb`**,
  **`FeiYin`** while mobs.json stores the apostrophes — **458 refs across 54 names fail an exact-string
  join** (`Crawlers' Nest` 33, `Ordelle's Caves` 29, `Carpenters' Landing` 27, `King Ranperre's Tomb` 23).
  zones.json is not even consistent with itself: `Ru'Lude Gardens` and `Southern San d'Oria` keep theirs.
  **But audit.py has had `ZONES_NORM = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", z.lower())` since it was written**, which
  is why it reports **14** unresolved, not 54 — and the 14 are the genuine free zones (Apollyon, Temenos,
  Nyzul, the Odin/Brunhilde chambers). **Nothing is broken today**: `MobZoneRow` renders the mob's own
  string and the Zones mode groups on it, so mobs.json never joins ZoneDb. **The rule that matters: the
  canon for a mob's `zones` is mobs.json's own dominant form, and any future mob->ZoneDb link MUST
  normalise the way audit.py does.** See §8. Open (cq).
- **`zones` IS A LIST OF `[zone, "lv range"]` PAIRS, NOT A LIST OF STRINGS** — 2,186 pairs / 685 bare
  `[zone]` / **19 flat strings** (the Behemoth family) that the parser tolerates but nothing else writes.
  `MobRow` reads element 1 under a zone header, so **a per-zone level range is a real, rendered field.**
  It also resolved the Hati conflict below without a fudge. Some entries are `[zone, null]` (abhac).
- **THE HATI CONFLICT — AND THE PER-ZONE RANGE IS WHY THE UNION RULE DID NOT APPLY.** Adversaries says
  `Hati` 77-79 in King Ranperre's Tomb; the file says **lv [135, 137]** with a 16-min respawn (Apex
  shape). They do not overlap, so this is a contradiction, not a "the file's span is wider" case. The
  union would have rendered a **60-level span** in the family view and said nothing the zone entry does
  not already carry -> **kept lv [135,137], put `77-79` on the zone.** Both facts survive, each where it
  renders. Open (cr).
- **BOREAL HOUND CARRIES A FULL 12-CELL ALTERNATIVE GRID AND WAS EXEMPTED FROM THE FAMILY STAMP** —
  Fire/Light **+87.5%**, Slashing +68.8%, all other melee and elements +50%, Ice/Dark +30%. Internally
  consistent, page-shaped, and **it contradicts itself against the leftover `st: [[Dark,null],[Ice,null]]`
  stamp** (weak to Ice +30% *and* resistant to Ice). The Defiant/Corse precedent says a per-mob published
  grid stays -> **stamped nothing over it.** Needs its page. Open (cs).
- **A SEVENTH MARKUP FLAVOUR, AND IT IS ONE CHARACTER**: `Methane Breath`'s notes was **`":"`** — a bare
  colon. Not empty, so §9's empty-string guard scores it 0; not markup, so the detector misses it too.
  **A def whose notes is pure punctuation is a stub.** The def also had **no `el` at all** where the page
  paints it Fire.
- **I RE-DERIVED `Revival Tree Root` -> `Revival Root` FROM SCRATCH — AND REV 29 ALREADY HAD IT.** The
  DOOMED rev summary says *"Ledger (§7): wiki `Revival Tree Root` -> DB `Revival Root`"* — **but it was
  never actually added to the §7 ledger list**, so it was invisible to a reader who went where the doc
  told them to look. **Now filed there.** Second time in two revs that this doc already knew (Ghost:
  the Shadows column). **A finding announced in a rev header is not a finding you can find later —
  put it in the section it belongs to.**
- **THE ELEMENT ROW IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO GHOST'S** — Fire 150 / Wind 130 / Lightning 130 / Light 150 /
  Ice 50 / Earth 100 / Water 130 / Dark 50. Two Undead families, same eight cells. **Row 1 differs**:

## 1. What this project is

Complete the FFXI mob index in **MobileWatch** (native Android, Kotlin/Jetpack Compose) family-by-family
from BG-wiki screenshots, then port the finished data to **OmniWatch** and **WarnMe**.

The canonical data file is `app/src/main/assets/mobs.json` (~2.8 MB, compact single-line JSON).

**Workflow per family:**

1. User uploads BG-wiki screenshots: the category page (Bestiary box + resist grid + Abilities table +
   General Notes), the NM / Adversaries / Event-Appearances tables, the category page list, and a page per
   notable NM.
2. Inspect the existing records first — `fam == '<Family>'` — before writing anything.
3. Apply the **family stamp** (§6): resists, kit, crystal, job, detection, eco, family_notes.
4. Refine notable NMs individually from their own pages.
5. Fill `zones` from the Adversaries / NM / Event-Appearances tables.
6. Run every verifier in §9.
7. Rebuild and deliver the full zip (§10).
8. Write the family note to the running memory log.

**Priority order (user-stated):** abilities first — the name plus what it actually does (Target /
Physical-Magical / Element / Effect / Notes). Everything else is secondary.

---

## 2. READ THIS BEFORE YOU EDIT — verify the zip

The working copy at `/home/claude/android` does **not** persist across sessions. Re-extract with a guard,
never blindly:

```bash
cd /home/claude && (ls android/app/src/main/assets/mobs.json >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || unzip -q /mnt/user-data/uploads/MobileWatch-android.zip -d .)
```

`rm -rf android && unzip` has wiped in-progress work before. Don't.

**The uploaded zip can be stale.** On 2026-07-15 a whole family pass was lost: the user never received the
previous session's zip (the connection dropped), and `/mnt/user-data/outputs` *and* `/mnt/transcripts` were
both bare. Memory said the work was done; only the zip proves it.

**`/mnt/user-data/outputs` CAN BE NEWER THAN `/mnt/user-data/uploads`.** Hit for real on 2026-07-15: the
container survived a compaction, so the *previous* session's delivered zip was still sitting in `outputs/`
(21:13) while `uploads/` still held the base the user had sent at the *start* of that session (20:57).
Extracting from `uploads/` silently reverted the whole Flock Bat pass — zones 45→0, crys 52→22,
`family_eco` gone — and `audit.py` still came up green afterwards, because it audits whatever is in front
of it. **`ls -la` BOTH directories and take the newer zip.**

**So: at session start, pick 3-4 specific values the family log claims were changed and check them.**

```bash
python3 -c "import json; m=json.load(open('app/src/main/assets/mobs.json'))['mobs']; \
print(m['claret'].get('sub'), m['bedrock barry'].get('ab'), m['ironbeak inguza'].get('sub'))"
```

If they diverge from the log, **tell the user and ask for the right zip** before building on it.

## 3. Data model

### Top level

| key | shape |
|---|---|
| `mobs` | **DICT** keyed by lowercased mob name → mob dict (*not* a list) |
| `abilities` | name → `{d, t, r, tgt, fx[], el, notes}` |
| `families` | family list |
| `family_icons` | family → `<Family>.jpg` |
| `family_notes` | family → **array** of bullet strings |
| `family_subtypes` | family → `[{name, wk, st, notes, img}]` |
| `family_eco` | family → ecosystem |
| `family_resist_sets_pending` | parked colour sets; the app ignores it |

### Per-mob keys

`n fam lv[min,max] agg lnk nm ab[] sp[] det[] job resp crys wk st ab_el im sub eco zones notes spawn
drops nmlv img`

- `wk` / `st` — `[[type, delta]]`, e.g. `[["Fire","+30%"]]`
- `ab_el` — absorbed elements. **A LIST OF STRINGS, NEVER A BARE STRING** (MobDb.kt:157
  `absorb = strList(o,"ab_el")`, and `strList = optJSONArray(k) ?: emptyList()` — a string silently
  renders *no* absorb).
- `im` — immunities. `MobDb.kt:156 immune = strList(o,"im")`, rendered in the card's Details box.
- `el` on an **ability** is a plain **STRING** (`"Fire"`), never a list — the parser uses `optString`, so a
  list renders literally as `["Fire"]` on the card. Join multi-element as `"Fire/Ice"`.
- `drops` — a comma-joined **STRING**, not a list.
- `zones` — `List<[zone, "lv-range"?]>`

### Editing

```python
import json
d = json.load(open('mobs.json'))
# ... mutate ...
json.dump(d, open('mobs.json','w'), separators=(', ', ': '), ensure_ascii=False)
```

Companion **read-only** refs in the same folder:
`zones.json` (top-level key `zones` → list of `{name, slug, ...}`), `ffxi_items.json` (item names under key
`n`), `jobs.json` (`spellinfo` keys = valid spell names).

### Taxonomy (locked)

**Ecosystem** (= wiki "Type": Beast / Lizard / Bird / Amorph …, stored in `family_eco`)
→ **Type** (= `fam`: Behemoth, Coeurl, Antlion)
→ **Sub-type** (= `sub`) — **USER 2026-07-15: "rule isnt a different image gets a sub type, its more
a different set of resists or skills." A DIFFERENT RENDER IS NOT ENOUGH. The test is a different
RESIST SET or SKILL SET; the model is corroboration, not the criterion.**
→ individual mob.

`fam` is the **specific family**, never the ecosystem.

## 4. !! Explicit JSON `null` is poison — AND THE SHAPE MUST MATCH THE ACCESSOR !!

### !!!! A WRONG CONTAINER SHAPE = ZERO MOBS, SILENTLY. Skeleton, rev 35-38. !!!!
`family_subtypes["Skeleton"]` was written as an **object** where the schema says **list**. `MobDb.load`
calls `so.getJSONArray(f)`; org.json throws typeMismatch; `AuctionViewModel` swallows it with
**`runCatching { MobDb.load(app) }.getOrNull()`**; `mobDb` is null; every list is `?: emptyList()`.
**The app showed no mobs at all — browse, filter and search — for four revs, with no crash and no log
line.** `optJSONArray`/`optString` are forgiving; **`getJSONArray`/`getJSONObject`/`getString` are not,
and load() uses them in nine places.** THE RULE: **before writing a container, check the Kotlin accessor
that reads it** (the `ab_el`-as-string bug and the null-poison bug are the same failure class).
**audit.py §2 now simulates every strict call in load() — it must read 0. Run it before every zip.**

### The original rule

**NEVER write `None` values into mobs.json.**

Android's `org.json` `optString(k)` returns the **literal string `"null"`** for a key whose value is JSON
null. So `o.optString("eco").ifBlank{null}` yields `"null"` — *not* blank — and
`mob.eco ?: familyEcoMap[...]` never falls back. The browser then renders a group header literally titled
**"null"**. An *absent* key returns `""` → `ifBlank` → `null` → correct fallback.

**A key with value null and an absent key are IDENTICAL in Python** (`m.get(k)` is `None` for both). You
must test `'k' in m`, not `m.get(k) is None`. This is what made the bug survive two "the data is fine"
verdicts.

Fixed 2026-07-14: 586 null-valued keys stripped (`eco` 4 = the original Yggdreant bug; `sub` 192 → "null"
sub-type headers; `el` 45 + `r` 10; `img` 14, including `family_subtypes['Yztarg']` White Yztarg whose
`img: null` defeated the family-icon fallback; `drops`/`job`/`crys` 10).

**Safe — do NOT strip:** the deliberate `[type, null]` pairs *inside* `wk`/`st` arrays. The Kotlin reads
those with `!e.isNull(1)`, which is correct. Array fields (`wk st ab det lv zones notes`) use
`optJSONArray`, which is null-safe. Only `optString` fields are vulnerable: mob
`n fam job crys spawn drops nmlv sub eco img`, ability `d t r tgt el notes`, subtype `name img`.

**Guard after every single edit:**

```python
assert not [k for m in d['mobs'].values() for k,v in m.items() if v is None]
```

### `notes` on a mob is a **LIST OF STRINGS**, not a string — Rockfin, 2026-07-16

`MobDb.kt` reads it as `notes: List<String>`. The parse line tolerates both —
`optJSONArray("notes") ?: optString("notes").ifBlank{null}?.let{listOf(it)}` — so a string does **not**
crash and does **not** vanish. It renders as **one giant bullet** instead of one bullet per point, which
is why this is easy to ship without noticing. **652 records carry a list; the only 3 strings the file has
ever had were written in this very pass and caught by the new §9 verifier before shipping.**

Same shape as the `ab_el` bare-string trap, one field over: the type is not enforced, so the only defence
is the verifier. `family_notes[fam]` is a list of bullets too.

**Root-cause hardening (offered, NOT done — user's call):** add a MobDb helper
`fun str(o,k) = if (o.isNull(k)) null else o.optString(k).ifBlank{null}` and route every `optString`
through it. Kotlin can't be compiled in this environment.

## 5. Reading a BG-wiki page

### Resist grid — 2 rows of 8

- **TOP (damage types):** Physical, Magical, Breath, Slashing, **Blunt (= data "Impact")**, H2H, Piercing,
  Ranged
- **BOTTOM (elements):** Fire, Wind, Lightning, **Light**, Ice, Earth, Water, Dark

#### !!!! FIND THE CATEGORY PAGE MECHANICALLY BEFORE YOU READ ANYTHING — Vampyr, 2026-07-17 !!!!

**Rev 34 recorded a Vampyr screenshot as "the category page, grid + full ability table". It was Lord
Varney's mob page.** Nothing was written from it, but a whole pass was planned on it. A mob page and a
category page look alike: both have a General Notes box, a render, an info box and an ability table.

**The discriminator is the element row, and it is one scan:** a family grid is the only thing on BG with
**all eight element gems within ±6px of a single horizontal row**. Reference RGBs (measured, stable
across renders):

| gem | RGB | tell |
|---|---|---|
| Fire | `(220,178,24)` | hue 47, sat .89 |
| Wind | `(77,156,143)` | hue 170 |
| Lightning | `(41,8,194)` | hue 250, sat .96 — the most saturated cell |
| **Light** | `(182,150,160)` | **hue 341, sat .18 — the DESATURATED one** |
| Ice | `(108,102,215)` | hue 243, val .84 |
| Earth | `(136,120,17)` | hue 51, val .53 |
| Water | `(88,147,161)` | hue 191 |
| Dark | `(137,73,137)` | hue 300 |

Run it over a whole batch: the category pages score **8/8**, every mob page and listing scores **<=6**.
It found `...678167` (Category:Vampyr) in one pass and cannot be fooled by a page that merely looks like
one. **Do this first on every new batch.** (It also confirms the locked element order above — Vampyr and
Skeleton both re-derived Fire/Wind/Lightning/Light/Ice/Earth/Water/Dark from these hues alone.)

#### THE GRID READER IS MECHANICAL — OCR the magnitude, MEASURE the direction. 16/16 on a blind control.

Do not eyeball percentages. Per cell:
1. **Direction — ink colour, and it is never wrong.** Take the sub-620-sum pixels and average them:
   green channel leading = **weak**, red leading by 40+ = **resist**, neither = **neutral (100%)**.
   Scored **16/16** against a grid already read by eye.
2. **Magnitude — OCR at `--psm 7`** with whitelist `0123456789.%ASR`. Scored **14/16**.
3. **!! THE TWO MISSES ARE ALWAYS THE HALF-TIERS. !!** `87.5%` and `112.5%` are wider than the 36.6px
   column and clip to `7.5%` / `12.5%`. **Padding the crop is NOT the fix** — it drags in the
   neighbour's digits (`5100%1`, `515%8`). **Re-OCR the clipped cell alone at `--psm 8` and `--psm 13`
   and require them to agree.** That is what settled Vampyr's Magical cell: `13%` at psm 7, **`75%`** at
   psm 8 *and* 13.
4. Cross-check: a true 100% cell scores ~52 red (the `%` glyph) + ~31 black (the digits) — the Naraka
   ink test, still valid.

Damage-type resists are stored exactly like elements: `["Magical","-25%"]`.
`delta = wiki% - 100` → 130 → `+30%`, 70 → `-30%`, 10 → `-90%`. Half-tiers are fine: 112.5 → `+12.5%`.

- `[type, null]` renders a green "Weak" / red "Res" with **no number** — use it for **"S"** cells rather
  than guessing a magnitude.
- **A "?" CELL IS NOT DATA — DON'T RECORD IT.** "?" means unknown; `[type, null]` would assert a direction
  you don't have.
- **An all-"?" grid = the page has no grid data at all** → keep the family stamp. (Hugemaw Harold,
  Allergorhai, Sallow Seymour, lustful lydia, sensual sandy.)

### !!!! PROVENANCE PROSE NEVER GOES IN A `notes` FIELD — USER, 2026-07-16 !!!!

**The user sent a screenshot of Aquarius's card reading *"Its page publishes no resist grid — the values
here are the family stamp."* and said: *"i dont need this kind of info in the notes. if a specific mob
doesnt have a table, just fall back to family table, but we dont need explanations of it in the mobs
card."***

**EVERYTHING IN THIS DOC ABOUT WHERE DATA CAME FROM BELONGS IN THIS DOC — NOT IN mobs.json.** A note
field is player-facing. It answers *"what does this mob do to me?"*, never *"where did BalladOfWorms get
this number?"*.

**Four surfaces render on the mob card — all four were polluted:**

| surface | renders where |
|---|---|
| `mob.notes` | General Notes section (AuctionApp.kt:624) |
| sub-type `notes` | General Notes, same list (`vm.subtypeNotes`) |
| `family_notes` | General Notes, **on EVERY card in the family** (`vm.familyNotes`) |
| **ability def `notes`** | **under the description when an ability row is expanded (AuctionApp.kt:942)** — the one that is easy to forget |

**Swept 2026-07-16** (`meta_sweep.py`, kept in `_project/`): **204 bullets removed, 106 trimmed, 21
ability notes removed, 93 trimmed**; mob.notes 2,201 -> 2,007, family_notes 264 -> 238, ability notes
503 -> 482. Detector = a provenance/wiki-layout vocabulary applied **clause by clause**, so
`"<game fact>. <meta sentence>"` keeps the fact.

**Out, always:** the family stamp, what a page publishes or leaves blank, `'?'` cells, rose shading, the
category/NM/Adversaries/Listings tables, column and cell names, the import, the old def, what was
undefined or left unset, NCC/IoU/pixel measurements, open-item references, dates, and cross-mob
comparisons ("the only Crab that publishes a grid").

**In, always:** what the mob does. Behaviour, phases, procs, gates ("Hoof Volley is used by Notorious
Monsters only" — the GATE is a game fact; *"gated by a parenthetical in its own name cell"* is not),
spawn conditions, HP, titles, drops-in-prose.

**If a mob has no grid of its own it just gets the family stamp — silently. That is the system working;
it is not a fact about the mob.**

**FOUR TRAPS, all hit while writing the sweep — the same over-broad-pattern class as the `sat > 60` gem
threshold and the `[:4]`-truncated drop search:**
1. **`\brow\b` ate `"twice in a row"`**; `stamped` (unbounded) ate **`"Title: Glavoid Stampeder"`**.
   Word-boundary every marker, then test it against real prose.
2. **Splitting clauses on `" - "` broke ZONE NAMES** — `"Dynamis - Qufim"`, `"Escha - Zi'Tah"`,
   `"Sheol - Gaol"`. Split on `;` and the em dash only.
3. **`"!!"` is the FFXI proc marker, not punctuation** — a sentence splitter on `[.!?]` truncates
   `"Silence triggers the blue !!"`. Same for `HP.` / `M.DEF.` as false abbreviations.
4. **Attribution PREFIXES hide real facts**: *"Pakecet's page adds that Angry Seas is what SUMMONS its
   adds..."*, *"The Sea Monk category table publishes the potency as 5~8 HP per tick"*. Deleting the
   sentence deletes the mechanic. **Strip the prefix, keep the fact** — but not when the prefix ends in a
   possessive (`"The category's Target column"` -> `"'s Target column"`).

**And the residue rule that matters most: only style-judge a fragment you actually CUT.** An untouched
bullet comes back byte-identical — otherwise the sweep "fixes" prose it has no business touching.

### A NOTE FIELD CAN BE A STRING WHERE THE SCHEMA SAYS LIST — Manticore, 2026-07-16

`family_subtypes['Manticore']` -> Legendary Manticore's `notes` was **a bare string**, not a list of
bullets. It renders fine (MobDb.kt:231-232 falls back to `optString(...).let{listOf(it)}`), so nothing
was visibly broken — but every Python pass that iterates `notes` walks it **character by character**.
Normalised to a list. It was the only one in the file; `mob.notes` and `family_notes` are clean.
**Same family as the `ab_el`-as-string bug: check the shape, not just the value.**

### A FIFTH FLAVOUR OF WIKI MARKUP IN A DEF — 2026-07-16

Four ability `notes` were pure markup: **`"**"`** (Orogenic Storm, Enervating Grasp) and
**`"*See also: Panzerschreck"` on the Panzerschreck def itself** (and Panzerfaust on Panzerfaust) — a
"see also" pointing at its own subject. The §5 detector (`__NOTOC|===|\{\{|\[\[`) misses both. Deleted.

### FLAVOURS 7, 8 AND 9 — AND THE FIELD THE DETECTOR WASN'T LOOKING AT — Acrolith, 2026-07-17

The detector reported **0** while four defs held markup:
- **`==How to Obtain==`** (`Sinker Drill`'s notes) — the regex had `===`, so a **level-2 heading** walked
  through. Match `==`, not `===`.
- **`'''`** (`Tail Smash`'s `d` and `Shell Charge`'s `d`) — wiki **bold**. `Tail Smash` is on 26 mobs.
- **`*Notes:`** — sitting in **`Arm Cannon`'s `r` field**, i.e. in the *range* slot, which the detector
  never read. **Scan `r` and `tgt`, not just `d`/`notes`.**

Current regex (audit.py §3, rev 36):
`__NOTOC|==|\{\{|\[\[|File:|thumb\||\d+px|none\||'''|\{\||^\*|<br` over `d + notes + r + tgt`.

**Nine flavours, five families, and not one was found by reading a def on purpose — every one came from
widening the net after a different family tripped over it. Widen it again the next time you touch it.**

### !! COUNTING A CATEGORY: FOUR THINGS THAT ARE IN A MOB CATEGORY BUT ARE NOT MOBS !!

Before you report an N:N-1 mismatch, ask what KIND of page the extra one is:

| class | example | tell |
|---|---|---|
| a `User:` **sandbox** | `User:Favre/Sandbox/GaolGuide` (Tulfaires, Waktza) | the `User:` namespace |
| a **dual-tag** | `Martinet` — Corpselight **and** Doll (Corpselight, 2026-07-16) | its own page's category line names both |
| a **battlefield / event** page | **`Totentanz`** — `Categories: Battlefields`, the Boneyard Gully ENM (Corse, 2026-07-16) | **it sorts out of alphabetical order** (Totentanz sits under **C**, next to `Corse`), because somebody gave it a sortkey; and the **Event Appearances table names it in the *Event* column**, not the Name column |
| an **Adversaries-only mob with no page** | `Eschan Corse` (Corse) — pushes the count the *other* way | its Adversaries row is **plain text, not a blue link** |

The last one is the mirror image: **a family can have MORE records than category pages and still be
right.** Corse = **25 pages − 1 battlefield = 24 mob pages = our 24 records**, **+ `eschan corse` folded
off the Adversaries table = 25 records.** Fold those orphans (§13) — `fam == X` loops skip them.

### !!!! PROSE NEXT TO AN ABILITY NAME IS NOT ITS ELEMENT — Vidmapire/Vampyr, 2026-07-17 !!!!

**The inverse of the Corse rule below, and far more dangerous, because it reads like a gift.** Vidmapire's
General Notes list every one of its TP moves with an inline element gem:

> *Bloodrake: (fire) **Fire**, en-Plague and Blaze Spikes · Decollation: (lightning) **Thunder** ·
> Eternal Damnation: (ice) **Ice** · Heliovoid: (earth) **Earth** · Nocturnal Servitude: (dark) **Dark**
> · Nosferatu's Kiss: (water) **Water** · Wings of Gehenna: (wind) **Wind***

Nine moves, nine elements, in words, on the wiki. **All but one of them is wrong for the ability.** Read
the rest of the box: *"Vidmapire changes its current elemental alignment after using TP moves... **You may
encourage these TP moves to be used by dealing primarily magical damage of their associated element**"* —
and its Condition column says *"Takes primarily (X) magical damage."* on every row. **The list is which
element you nuke it with to make it use the move.** It is a spawn condition for the move, not the move's
element.

**Measured, and the pixels are unambiguous** — its own Type column's 2nd icon vs its own prose:

| move | prose says | Type column measures | distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eternal Damnation | Ice | **Dark** | **0.0** |
| Nocturnal Servitude | Dark | **Light** | **0.0** |
| Nosferatu's Kiss | Water | **Dark** | **0.0** |
| Wings of Gehenna | Wind | Wind | 5 |

Three of four contradict, at distance 0.0 from the reference gem. **And the Category:Vampyr table's Type
column publishes the same four elements as Vidmapire's Type column** — the two tables agree with each
other and both disagree with the prose. Only Wings of Gehenna matches, by coincidence.

**THE TYPE COLUMN IS THE AUTHORITY FOR `el`. ALWAYS.** Prose is a source for *notes*, and for gates that
name mobs, and for grid words (Hahava). **It is not a source for an ability's element** — not even when
it is right there in a bulleted list with the gem drawn next to it.

### An element can be published in the DESCRIPTION cell — Corse/Envoutement, 2026-07-16

`Envoutement`'s Type column is the bare red Physical disc with **no element gem**, which this section has
always read as *"no element"*. It is not. **Awoken Andhrimnir's table writes the damage as "Deals ⬤
damage + Curse" with an inline gem** — matched against that page's own labelled grid gems it is **Dark at
distance 0.0** — and Giltine's prose independently says *"Darkness damage and Curse"*.

**Rule: "no 2nd icon in the Type column" means the TYPE COLUMN is silent, not that the move has no
element. Scan the description cell for gems too.** (The colour-match method is the same; the reference
gems are the same page's resist grid.)

### A mob page can carry the FAMILY table as BOILERPLATE — Corse/Awoken Andhrimnir, 2026-07-16

`Awoken Andhrimnir`'s **Abilities** section lists **all seven** Corse moves and labels three of them
**"(NM only)"** — on a mob whose own Adversary box reads **Class: Monster**. A table that gates rows
against a flag *its own subject does not have* is a copy of the family table.

**Tells that a per-mob ability table is boilerplate:** it carries **gate annotations** (`(NM only)`,
`(NMs only)`); it is the **full family kit**; its `Type` cells are all `?` while the category's are
painted. **Tells that it is real** (Muut, same batch): it is **shorter** than the family kit, and it
**disagrees with the category** — Muut's table paints Final Retribution's disc **red** where the category
paints it purple, which is somebody writing that row for that mob.

**Filed Awoken Andhrimnir with the base four. But the boilerplate is not worthless — it is what named the
rose gate** (see below).

### Ability Type column — the four category circles

**All four are confirmed** (the Leech page shows three side by side):

| colour | type |
|---|---|
| red | **Physical** |
| purple | **Magical** |
| **blue** | **Breath** |
| green | **Buff / heal** |

So BG *does* have a Breath icon and it is blue. The Morbol breath moves genuinely are painted
purple/Magical on their pages. **The user ruled "keep breaths as is" — do not re-raise this.**

### Ability element — colour-match the 2nd icon

Match against the **labelled element gems in that same page's resist grid** (identical styling). Sample the
dominant saturated RGB, pick nearest:

```
Fire(166,111,48)  Wind(59,128,116)  Lightning(91,52,150)  Ice(129,124,212)
Earth(135,123,45) Water(88,134,148) Dark(96,44,96)
```

**LIGHT IS THE TRAP.** It is a pale, desaturated pink-white ≈ **(195,168,177)**. The old
"near-white (230,230,230)" reference **mis-sorts it to Ice**. Rule: **lowest saturation wins.**

Calibration (measured):

| cell | mean saturation |
|---|---|
| blank / no icon | **~1** |
| **Light gem** | **~9-11** |
| any other element | **~33-58** |

So a saturated-pixel sampler returning **NO-ICON is itself the tell for Light** — check the raw mean before
concluding "no element". No 2nd icon at all = no element (physical melee / status-only).

### Shadows column

`1`/`2-3`/`4` = shadows consumed. **B** = bypasses but does not remove. **R** = removes all shadows.

### Condition column — **it can be a KIT GATE**

Not always flavour. Bat's table reads "CoP/ToAU only" on Marrow Drain and Subsonics, and "ToAU only" on
Supersonics — so base-game bats genuinely have a three-move kit. Confirmed independently by Tiyanak's and
Leucippe's own Listings (both omit Supersonics). **Read this column.**

### The BLACK Type disc — **two families now, and it is not what Pteraketos guessed**

**Pteraketos, 2026-07-16** found a fifth category glyph: a pure-greyscale disc (max saturation 1) in the
Type cell's first slot, on **Thar She Blows**, the table's only instant-KO move. That coincidence was the
only hint, and (bd) recorded it.

**Rockfin, 2026-07-16 — the hint is dead.** The same glyph (mean RGB `(41,41,41)`, **max saturation
1.5%**) sits on **Carcharian Verve, a pure self-buff that deals no damage at all**, and it is there on
**three independent tables** — the category page, Tchakka's page and Dakuwaqa's page. An instant-KO conal
and a self-buff do not share a damage category. Whatever the disc encodes, it is not "Death".

**What Rockfin adds that Pteraketos could not see:**

| table | Carcharian Verve's Type cell |
|---|---|
| Rockfin category | **BLACK** + **green Buff** |
| Tchakka's page | **BLACK** + **green Buff** |
| Dakuwaqa's page | **BLACK** alone |
| Ngai's page | **purple Magical** alone (and "Buff" in its *Area* cell) |

The green disc's hue is **152.8°** against Pugil's Water Shield Buff disc at **152.0°** — the same icon.
So **the row does carry a documented category after all**; it is just sitting in the second slot with the
black disc in the first. `t: "Buff"` was set from it. **That is the practical lesson: when slot 1 is the
black disc, read slot 2 before giving up on `t`** — Pteraketos left Thar She Blows' `t` unset and its
slot 2 was empty, so nothing was lost there.

The black disc's inner glyph is also **structurally different**: the red/purple/green/blue discs all carry
the same triangle, the black one carries a small lattice. It is a distinct icon, not a greyed-out known
one. **Still unexplained; (bd) stays open** with the hint removed and the co-occurrence added.

**!!!! NARAKA, 2026-07-17 — 3rd SIGHTING, AND THE FIRST WHERE THE MOVE'S NATURE IS NOT IN DOUBT. !!!!**
Vinipata's own ability table paints **Raksha Stance** and **Yaksha Stance** with the disc (16x16, pure
greyscale, R=G=B throughout, black rim, symmetric lat/long mesh, max sat 7.1). **Both are self-targeting
stances that grant the MONSTER -50% damage taken and erase its ailments — and they are the ONLY two rows
in that table with `Target: Self`.** The legend's 4th Type is literally **Buff**. So the disc means Buff,
unless §5's `green = Buff/heal` (confirmed on Leech, three side by side) is right — **in which case the
disc is a FIFTH icon.** Both cannot be true. **What would settle it: one page showing a green Type icon
and the disc together, or an alt-text read (the Fomor method).** Meanwhile the CATEGORY table paints
both Stances **purple/Magical**, which is worse than useless for a move that deals no damage — **`t`
left UNSET on both.** Open (cu).

### Row colour, part 2 — **the BLUE row is a RENDERING ARTIFACT. Solved 2026-07-16 (Pugil).**

**Pteraketos, 2026-07-16** first turned up a third background in an ability-table name column:
`(201,205,224)` **blue** on Deep Sea Dirge, against normal `(239,238,238)` and rose `(224,206,206)`. It
could not mean "restricted" — *every* member of the family published the move — so it went into §12 as
open (bc), unexplained.

**Pugil, 2026-07-16 — SOLVED, and (bc) is closed.** Two screenshots of the **same** category ability table,
taken minutes apart in one session, **disagree about the same cell**:

| capture | Aqua Ball name cell |
|---|---|
| first | `(239,238,238)` normal |
| second | `(201,205,224)` **blue** |

No data changed between them. The blue is the **CSS `:hover` highlight — the reader's own mouse**
(user, 2026-07-16: *"the blue artifact is because im hovering over it when i screenshot it"*). This doc
guessed `:target`/anchor for two revs; the tells below were all correct, the mechanism was not.
Two independent tells, either of which is enough:

1. **It moves between captures of the same table.** Data does not.
2. **It fills every data cell across the full width of the row** (x=24..941, both sub-rows). That is
   exactly the Ongo test: *colour that reaches the data cells is rendering; a real rose gate shades only
   the ability's NAME cell, across both of the row's sub-rows.*

Deep Sea Dirge was the same artifact, and (bc)'s own counter-evidence — all four members publish it — was
the tell all along. **Rose remains real; blue is noise.** The Ongo test is the one to run, and it now has a
second, cleaner confirmation.

**Third sighting — Rockfin/Ngai, 2026-07-16, and the first on a MOB page rather than a category page.**
Ngai's 13-row table shades Protolithic Puncture `(201,205,224)` across **x=13..930 — the full table
width**, every data cell included. Same colour, same full-width fill, different page, different family.
The artifact is now confirmed three times. **Sample the row background, then run the Ongo test on it; if
the colour reaches the data cells, ignore it.**

**Fourth sighting — Ruszor/Scylla, 2026-07-16 — and the user closed the whole thing.** Scylla's Hydro Wave
row is `(201,205,224)` across **every data cell** while its **name cell stays `(239,238,238)`** — the exact
inverse of a rose gate, and exactly what a row highlight paints when the name cell is `rowspan=2` (the
highlight owns one `<tr>`; the name cell belongs to both sub-rows and keeps its own background).

**IT IS THE MOUSE.** User, 2026-07-16: *"the blue artifact is because im hovering over it when i screenshot
it"* — CSS `:hover`, i.e. **the cursor of the person taking the screenshot**. That is why it moves between
two captures of one table, why it never correlates with any data, and why it lands on a different row every
time. **Four sightings, one cause, and the cause is not on the wiki at all.**

**Nothing about the reading rule changes: rose = name cell only. Blue = anything else -> ignore it.**
It is now also a **free tell about the screenshot rather than the data** — a blue row is simply the row the
user was pointing at.

### !!!! THE ADVERSARIES TABLE'S HOVER IS **ROSE**, NOT BLUE — USER, 2026-07-16. MEASURE THE WIDTH. !!!!

**User, about `Wayward Dullahan`'s rose row in the Dullahan *Adversaries* table: *"the rose row is my
hovering with the cursor"*.** He is right, and it closes the last gap in the rose story.

Every rose/blue block across the session's 26 screenshots, measured:

| screenshot | table | tint | width | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Palloritus | **ability** (grey hdr `75,77,79`) | BLUE `(201,205,224)` | **688 px** | full row -> **cursor** |
| Crom Dubh | **ability** (grey hdr) | BLUE `(201,205,224)` | **917 px** | full row -> **cursor** |
| **Dullahan** | **Adversaries** (maroon hdr `157,87,87`) | **ROSE** `(224,206,206)` | **917 px** | full row -> **CURSOR** |
| Doomed category | **ability** (grey hdr) | ROSE `(224,206,206)` | **227 px** | name cell only -> **GATE** |
| Dullahan category | **ability** (grey hdr) | ROSE `(224,206,206)` | **227 px** | name cell only -> **GATE** |

**THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE WIDTH, NOT THE COLOUR:**
1. **FULL ROW (600-920 px, every cell) = THE CURSOR.** Its **colour follows the table's palette** —
   **BLUE** in the grey-headered ability tables, **ROSE** in the maroon-headered Adversaries table.
   **Rose and blue are one phenomenon in two skins.**
2. **NAME CELL ONLY (~227 px = the Ability column's width; Type/Area/Target/Condition stay
   `(239,238,238)`) = the real gate.** It bleeds into the description row at the *same x range* because
   the name cell is `rowspan=2`. **Both gates measured this session are 227 px on the nose.**

**MEASURE THE BLOCK'S WIDTH BEFORE READING ANY TINT.** The Ongo test was always doing this — it just
tested extent per-row instead of measuring the block, and it only ever ran on ability tables.

**THIS IS THE REAL CAUSE OF THE COCKATRICE MISREADING**, corrected below: "rose = Abyssea" came from
**Cluckatrice's row in the Cockatrice *Adversaries* table** — a full-width **cursor** in a maroon table —
sitting on the same page as the Cockatrice *ability* table's three genuine name-cell gates. **Same
colour, two tables, two meanings, one page.** Colibri and Flock Bat refuted the conclusion; only the
width measurement explains where it came from.

**(bc) and (cn) are the same open and both are CLOSED. There is one artifact: the mouse.**

#### !!!! THE REFERENCE CASE — QUTRUB, 2026-07-17: BOTH ARTIFACTS, ONE TABLE, ONE SCREENSHOT !!!!

**If this ever gets re-argued, cite this page and stop.** The Qutrub category **ability** table (grey
header) carries the cursor and the gate at the same time:

| row | tint | count at the MAIN row | x span | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Fortifying Wall` | BLUE `(201,205,224)` | **868 px** | full row | **CURSOR** |
| `Unblest Jambiya`, `Gen'ei Ryodan`, `Phantom Whorl`, `Triple Reversal`, `Enforce` | ROSE `(224,206,206)` | **228 px** | **x 28-255 only** | **GATE** |

Three things this nails down that no earlier page did:
1. **The gate is ROSE in a GREY-headered table.** The palette rule above is about the *cursor* only —
   it does not predict the gate's colour. Do not reason "grey table, so rose must be the cursor".
2. **228 px, the same figure Naraka measured.** Two families, two sessions, one number. The Ability
   column is 228 px wide and a gate fills exactly it.
3. **!! THE CURSOR'S BLUE ALSO BLEEDS 228 px INTO THE DESCRIPTION ROW !!** — `Fortifying Wall`'s
   description row (y=152) scores **228 blue px at x 28-255**, identical in shape to a gate, because the
   name cell is `rowspan=2` and the hover tints it in both rows. **MEASURE THE MAIN ROW.** A naive
   per-row scan that happens to land on a description row will report a gate that is a mouse.
   (This is the Scylla note — *"the name cell stays clean while every data cell goes blue"* — from the
   other side, and it is why a whole-column scan must group rows into ability blocks first.)

| Flock Bat | 69 | Abyssea-Tahrongi / -Vunkerl |
| Corse | 29 | Abyssea-Attohwa / -Tahrongi |
| Doomed | 27 | Abyssea-Attohwa |
| **Dullahan** | 12 | **NO — not in Abyssea at all** (and it roses `Noahionto`) |
| **Tulfaires** | 4 | **NO — not in Abyssea at all** (and it roses `From the Skies`) |

**Two families carry a rose gate and have zero Abyssea presence.** That kills "rose = Abyssea" outright,
without needing Broxa's release date or Tres Duendes' forms. **Use this one.**

**AND HERE IS WHERE THE WRONG IDEA CAME FROM.** Cockatrice alone suggested it, because an identical rose
sat on that page's one Abyssea **Adversaries** row (Cluckatrice). **That rose was the user's CURSOR** —
the Adversaries table's hover tint is rose, not blue (see the width rule above). It was never a gate and
it was never about Abyssea. Colibri killed the conclusion at the time by a longer road: its Adversaries
table has **no** rose row at all, and Broxa is a **Delve** NM (post-Abyssea) that does *not* get the rose
moves. The rule that fits all three families is **"rose = restricted, not part of the standard kit"** —
the wiki does not say *whose* kit it is in, only that it is not everyone's. (Flock Bat is the one case where
something else in the file *does* say whose: the two rose rows are Tres Duendes' 2nd- and 3rd-form moves.)

**RUSZOR ADDS A THIRD: ROSE MARKS THE MOVE, NOT THE MOB — it carries onto the owner's own page.**
Ruszor roses **Aqua Cannon** and **Ice Guillotine** (name cells `(224,206,206)`, data cells
`(239,238,238)` — a clean Ongo test on both the category table *and* Scylla's). **Scylla is the owner**:
its Listings Abilities column publishes both, and its General Notes say outright that it *"has access to
all Ruszor TP moves"*. Its own page **still shades them rose anyway**, identically to the category. So a
rose row on a mob's own page is **not** the page telling you that mob is excluded — the shading is a
property of the move within the family, reproduced by the template wherever the row appears. Read the
Listings column and the prose, not the shading, to decide who owns it. (The 3 standard Ruszors kept the
un-rosed 5; Sedna's Abilities column is **blank**, not "None", so it kept the family 5 too.)

**GREATER BIRD ADDS A SECOND LESSON: rose can be a SWAP, not an ADD.** Its rose set is a 1:1 replacement of
the standard set — Gliding Spike→Dread Dive, Scratch→Blind Vortex, Triple Attack→Giga Scream,
Stormwind→Dread Wind — matched pair-for-pair on shadow count and Type. **Feather Barrier is un-rosed in
both tables**, i.e. shared. So do not assume rose rows are additional moves; check whether the un-rosed
rows pair off against them.

**AND THE SWAP IS PER-MOVE, NOT ALL-OR-NOTHING.** Published kits disagree with a blanket swap:
Suzaku keeps **Stormwind** (Feather Barrier / Dread Dive / Blind Vortex / Giga Scream / Stormwind /
Chainspell); Strix has **no wind move at all**; Kreutzet "uses standard Roc TP moves"; Gandji, Langmeidong
and Zacatzontli "use standard Greater Bird abilities"; Picolaton "**exclusively** uses the TP move
Stormwind". Rule applied: **a published Abilities column or a prose "uses standard X abilities" beats the
caption; the caption only fills NMs the wiki is silent about.**

Handling: **Colibri** was stamped with the 3 standard moves, rose moves added only where a page publishes
them; **Flock Bat** the same (4 standard on all 52, the 2 rose moves on Tres Duendes only). **Cockatrice was
stamped with all 8** under the old reading and is **the last family inconsistent with this** — open item (s).

### !! THE ROSE GATE WAS NAMED BY A PAGE — Corse, 2026-07-16 !!

Every family so far had to **infer** what rose means. Cockatrice guessed "Abyssea" (wrong). Colibri and
Flock Bat proved "restricted, owner unstated". **Corse settles the meaning:** its category table roses
**Gala Macabre, Final Retribution, Hadal Summons** — and **Awoken Andhrimnir's copy of that same table
labels exactly those three "(NM only)"**, in words. An independent editor of the same wiki wrote the
restriction out.

**So: rose = NOT the standard family kit. That is all it ever meant, and it is now sourced, not inferred.**
It still does not tell you *whose* kit — two of the three Corse rose rows carry their own Condition text
(*"Staff wielding Corses only"*, *"Purple Robe Corses (Kumakatok) only"*) that the `(NM only)` label does
not cover, and those gates name things the data cannot see (open (ce)).

Gala Macabre had no Condition text, so `(NM only)` **is** its gate and it was filtered on the `nm` flag —
the Corpselight/Corpse Breath precedent.

#### !!!! VAMPYR SETTLES WHAT ROSE MEANS, AND IT IS *NOT* "NM ONLY" — 2026-07-17 !!!!

**Read this before generalising from Qutrub or Corse.** Vampyr's category table roses **`Dirty Breath`,
`Minax Glare`, `Nocturnal Servitude`** — 167 px of tint inside **x 9-236, the name cell**, Condition
column **completely empty**, no blue anywhere on the table. Then **five pages name the users, and they do
not partition by NM at all**:

| page | class | published kit |
|---|---|---|
| **Wurdalak** | **`Class: Monster` — a STANDARD mob** | **exactly the six non-rose moves** |
| Vidmapire | Unity NM | the six **+ Nocturnal Servitude** |
| Lord Asag | Voidwatch NM | *"all Vampyr TP moves **except Dirty Breath**, but including Nocturnal Servitude"* -> six + Minax Glare + Nocturnal Servitude |
| Sava Savanovic | Geas Fete NM | *"**uses the following** TP moves"* -> six named, incl. **Dirty Breath + Minax Glare**, **not** Nocturnal Servitude |
| Lord Varney | NM | *"**Does not use Bloodrake** — so Blue Mages cannot learn it from him!"* -> five |

**Three NMs, three different rose subsets, and one of them (Sava) is missing a rose move another NM has.**
No `nm` filter reproduces this. **Rose means "NOT the standard family kit" and nothing more.** Corse's
`(NM only)` and Qutrub's `(NM only)` were **facts about Corse and Qutrub**, published in words on those
pages — they were never the rose's definition. **Where no page names the users, the honest stamp is the
un-rosed kit only**, which is what all 13 unpaged Vampyrs got.

#### The un-rosed-kit control group — now a PATTERN. Aynu-kaysey (rev 34), Wurdalak (rev 35).

Two families running, a **plain `Class: Monster` page has published exactly the non-rose rows and nothing
else**. That is the rose confirmed from the other side: not "here is what the rose moves are", but "here
is what the base kit is", written by someone else, landing on the same set.

**-> When a category table roses N rows, go find a `Class: Monster` page in that family. Its Abilities
column is the control group, and it is worth more than any amount of reasoning about the tint.**

#### Naming instance #4, and the first corroboration FROM THE OTHER SIDE — Qutrub, 2026-07-17

**Dimgruzub's own ability table** labels two of the five rose rows **`(NM only)`**: `Unblest Jambiya
(NM only, first weapon intact)` and `Gen'ei Ryodan (NM only)`. Fourth time an independent reader has put
the rose into words, fourth time it is the **generic restriction** and not a content type.

**But the better evidence is the negative one.** `Aynu-kaysey`'s page publishes a **six-row ability
table** — Animating Wail, Fortifying Wall, Hex Palm, Leaping Cleave, Mangle, Spinal Cleave — which is
**exactly the six non-rose rows of the category table, and nothing else**. Until now the rose was only
ever confirmed by pages naming what the rose moves *are*; this is a page publishing what the un-rosed kit
*is*, independently, and landing on the same six. **And its Adversary box says `Class: Monster`** — so the
`(NM only)` gate excludes it, and its own table agrees. Two unrelated fields on one page telling the same
story.

**-> the `(NM only)` filter ran on the `nm` flag (Gala Macabre precedent) MINUS aynu-kaysey**, whose own
page overrules a family-level gate (§6: "refine notable NMs individually — their own kit overrides").
When a mob's page and the family gate disagree, the page wins; that is not a "kit trim" and does not need
"exclusively uses X".

### A BLUE row is NOT a gate — it is a browser artifact

**Ongo, 2026-07-15 — settles the anomaly flagged on Harpeia's Wings of Woe.** Some rows render
blue-lavender `(201,205,224)`. It is **not** a fifth gate. Two independent proofs:

1. **It bleeds outside the name cell.** A real rose gate `(224,206,206)` shades **only the ability's name
   cell**, across both of the row's sub-rows; the data cells stay `(239,238,238)`. The blue instead fills
   the *whole* of exactly **one sub-row** — which is what a row highlight paints on a single `<tr>` when
   the name cell is `rowspan=2`. (Mechanism confirmed 2026-07-16: it is the reader's **`:hover`**.)
2. **The same ability is un-blued on the category page.** Crashing Thunder is blue on Ongo's table and
   plain grey on the Waktza category table. A data gate cannot flip between two pages of one family.

**So: sample the NAME CELL, not the row.** Rose in the name cell = gate. Colour that reaches the data
cells = rendering. Harpeia's Wings of Woe is the same artifact and is un-rosed and un-gated.

### Gate mechanism #4 — **the gate can be in the ABILITY NAME CELL**

Hippogryph's table has a row literally named **`Hoof Volley (NMs only)`**. Not a row colour, not the
Condition column, not prose in General Notes — the restriction is part of the name string. Kotan-kor Kamuy
(an NM) confirms it: its published kit is Jettatura + Hoof Volley and nothing else.

**So there are now four ways a BG table gates a move — and they do not co-occur:**

| # | mechanism | first seen |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | prose in General Notes ("uses standard X abilities", "unique TP move") | Colibri |
| 2 | the **Condition** column ("CoP/ToAU only") | Bat |
| 3 | **row colour** — rose `(224,206,206)` | Cockatrice |
| 4 | **a parenthetical in the ability name** — `(NMs only)` | Hippogryph |

Read all four before stamping a kit.

### Detection icons

| icon | value |
|---|---|
| red circular double-arrow | **Sight** |
| red speaker | **Sound** |
| red flame / sparkle | **Scent** |
| red "HP" glyph | **Blood** (= low-HP detection) |
| literal text "True Sig" | **True Sight** (never the arrow icon) |
| literal text "T(H)" | **True Sound** (True Hearing) |
| literal text "T(S)" | **True Sight** |
| **grey chain link** | **`lnk` — the family LINKS.** Not a detection; see below |

**The Detects box also carries a BEHAVIOUR flag — the grey chain = Links. Ruszor, 2026-07-16,
USER-CONFIRMED.** Ruszor's category Detects row is `[Sight arrow][Scent flame][grey chain link]` at
x=891 / 911 / 930. The first two are the documented red badges. The third is **greyscale**, visibly a
**chain link**, and matches nothing else in the table — the Amphiptere reference sheet (four glyphs side
by side) has no such icon, because those families' boxes evidently print no chain. It was filed as an open
question and the user closed it immediately: **"it does link"** -> `lnk: true` on all 5 Ruszors.

**What this unlocks:** `lnk` has been import-only for the whole project (3,465 true / 3,268 false, never
page-verified). **The chain is greyscale on purpose — it is not a detection, so it is not painted like
one** — and every category box that shows it is publishing that family's linking behaviour. **Check the
Detects cell for the chain on every future family.** Two cautions kept from the open item: a box with *no*
chain is not proof of *no* linking (blank != data, the standing rule), and this is one family — if a
second box shows a chain on a family the file says does **not** link, re-raise it.

**Aggressive has its own red badge and it lives in the mob-page Behavior column, not the Detects box** —
Scylla's Behavior cell paints `[Aggressive X][Sight arrow]`; Ruszor's category box publishes no Aggressive
glyph at all.

### !! DETECTION IS NOT AGGRESSION — never infer `agg` from a Detects box !!

**Ruszor, 2026-07-16 — a rule was written into this doc for one rev and the user killed it. It is
recorded here so nobody rebuilds it from the same evidence.**

The chain answer (*"it does link"*) made `lnk` readable off the box, and the obvious next inference is that
a box printing a *sense* means the mob acts on it. The user was asked and said **"yes, if it is sight /
sound or linking, its aggressive"** — which rev 17 generalised. He corrected it at once:

> **"the family can detect but not necessarily be aggressive. these mobs were though so its ok"**

**So the box publishes DETECTION, full stop.** A passive family still has senses; FFXI is full of mobs
that detect and never aggro. **`agg` comes from a page that says so** — the red **Aggressive** badge in a
mob page's Listings **Behavior** column — **or from the user.** Ruszor's `agg: true` on all 5 is his word
about those five, **not an inference from their box**, and it is the only reason it is filed.

| glyph in the Detects cell | what it gives you |
|---|---|
| red badges (Sight / Sound / Scent / Blood…) | `det` — **and nothing else** |
| grey chain | `lnk` — **and nothing else** |
| *(none of them)* | `agg` — it is not in this box |

**The 1,752-record `agg` back-fill is CLOSED, (br). DO NOT RUN IT.** And note what nearly happened: the
sweep was held back because `land crab` (lv 5-7, det Sound) is `agg: true` while `wild rabbit` (lv 1, det
Sight+Scent) has **no `agg` key** — read as the import contradicting itself. **It wasn't. That split is
the data being right**, and it is the cleanest evidence in the file that the two fields are independent.
When a would-be sweep's own counterexamples look like noise, they are usually the answer.

**A mob page's Behavior column is NOT a Detects box.** Scylla has no Detects row at all; its Listings
Behavior cell paints `[Aggressive X][Sight arrow]` (NCC **0.839** to the category's Sight glyph, so the
arrow is confirmed Sight a second way). That is a *subset* of the family's Sight+Scent, not a
contradiction — and the Ongo rule only lets a page override where it **contradicts**. So the family stamp
stood and Scylla kept Sight+Scent. Sedna's Behavior cell is a literal **`?`** = not data, same rule.
(Scylla's junk `True Sight`, the recurring bad import stamp, was stripped — no page publishes it.)

**`Blood` = low-HP detection** — confirmed file-wide: 510 mobs carry it, concentrated in the undead
families (Skeleton, Fomor, Ghost, Hound, Doomed, Corse, Qutrub, Vampyr). Amphiptere is the odd one out and
its own page says so: *"Can detect and aggro low HP despite not being undead."*

**NCC reference sheet:** the **Amphiptere category Detects box** shows all four glyphs side by side —
Sight / Sound / **Blood** / Scent — at `y=330-348, x=984 / 1006 / 1027 / 1049` in upload
`1784142762061_image.png`. The Slime category box is a clean lone **Sound** speaker; the Slug box's 2nd icon
is a confirmed **Scent**.

Verify ambiguous icons by **grayscale-normalized NCC** against a known ref. Auto-locate the red icon's bbox
first — loose crops give weak scores. A good match scores **~0.8-1.0**; a wrong one **~0.3**.

**Recurring bad stamp:** `['Sight', …, 'True Sight'/'True Sound']` from an early import. Clean it per family
to the real icon(s).

**Detection is NOT always family-uniform.** Lesser Bird's category box is a lone **Sight** arrow, and
Helldiver's and Habrok's own pages agree (NCC 1.0 against it) — but **Nunyenunc's and Piasa's Detects
boxes both publish the Sound speaker** (NCC 0.88 to each other, 0.29-0.32 vs Sight). Two pages
independently disagreeing with their own category is data, not error. Stamp the family, then let each
page that publishes a glyph override itself.

### The category / NM-summary table is systematically STALER than the mob's own page

**Twelve instances so far. ALWAYS PREFER THE MOB PAGE — and record both in notes.**

| mob | category table | own page |
|---|---|---|
| Argus, Leech King | respawn 18-30 hours | **1-2 hours** (Nov 5 2013 update) |
| Bloodsucker | every 72 hours | **every 1 hour** |
| Taisaijin | morph coord (G-5) | **(G-9)~(H-9)** |
| Mountain Worm (NM) | "approximately every 21 hours" | **21-24 hours** |
| Lil' Apkallu | Lv 82 | **80-85** |
| **Desmodont** | lottery off **Blade Bat** | lottery off **the Stink Bats** |
| **Roc** | timed every **21-24 hours** | **every 18 hours or less** (Nov 5 2013 patch) |
| **Simurgh** | timed every **21-24 hours** | **approximately every 1-2 hours** |
| **Piasa** | Lv **~80**, timed spawn at **(E-5)** | Lv **~85**, respawns every 10-15 min around the **(E-7)/(F-7)/(E-8)/(F-8)** corner |
| **Kotan-kor Kamuy** | file Lv **80**, `nmlv` **80-82** | Lv **84** |

Piasa is a **two-column** conflict — the level AND the coordinate — on a table that got both wrong.

Desmodont is a **placeholder** conflict, not a timer — the failure mode is broader than respawn times. Roc
and Simurgh landed on the same day from the same category table, and **both** of its spawn figures were
wrong in the same direction: treat that table's spawn column as unreliable, not merely stale.

### Blank vs "None"

BG writes **"None"** in the Abilities column when it means it (Bedrock Barry → `ab: []`, backed by prose
"Uses no TP Moves"). A **BLANK** column is just missing data → keep the family stamp (Trembler Tabitha).
Don't read blank as empty.

### A page can publish a MISSPELLED name — and contradict itself doing it

**Ruszor/Scylla, 2026-07-16.** Scylla's Listings **Spells** column reads **`Paralyzga`**. The *same
page's* General Notes read **`Paralyga`** — one screenshot, two spellings, ten centimetres apart.
`Paralyga` is the real spell and the only one of the two in `jobs.json`; `Paralyzga` is in nothing.
Filed `Paralyga`.

Same class as the wiki's `Frozen Myst` (Listings) vs **`Frozen Mist`** (the ability table, which is also
the link target), and `Sub-Zero Smash` vs **`Sub-zero Smash`**, both on that one page.

**Rule: when a page fights itself over a NAME, the reference file wins** — `jobs.json` for spells,
`ffxi_items.json` for drops. That is not the page-beats-scrape rule being overturned; the page is still
the authority on *what the mob does*. It is just not a speller. **Verifier 6 catches exactly this and it
is why it exists — do not "fix" a verifier miss by adding the typo to the data.**

### A '?' in a Bestiary row is not data either

Hugemaw Harold's page paints Job `?`. That's an explicit "unknown", so the family stamp stands — same rule
as a '?' resist cell. (Precedent for the other direction: toxic tamlyn → `'? / Black Mage'`.)

### An existing ability def is NOT a trustworthy def — read it against the page

The defs that came in with the import are as suspect as the resist stamps, and for the same reason: they
were scraped, not read (§15). **FIVE flavours of wiki markup have leaked into `d` / `notes`:**

| flavour | where it was caught |
|---|---|
| a **Clear Mind job-trait paragraph** pasted as the description | Slug's **Corrosive Ooze** — and **AGAIN on Sea Monk's `Maelstrom` 2026-07-16, in `notes` this time.** Two families, one paragraph: it is a **class**, not a one-off. **Prose, so check 8 is blind to it** — the only defence is reading the def against the page |
| `===Skillchain Properties===` | Apkallu's **Beak Lunge** + **Wing Slap** |
| `__NOTOC____NOTOC__` as the entire description | Bat's **Blood Drain** |
| a notes field ending `{{Verification` | **Virulent Haze** |
| **`d` = `"File:RendingDeluge.png"`** — the image filename instead of the text | Craklaw's **Rending Deluge**, found 2026-07-15; adding `File:` to the detector immediately caught **Diffusion Ray** too |
| **notes = `":"`** — a single colon, the whole field | Hound's **Methane Breath**, 2026-07-17. **Not empty (§9's empty-string guard scores it 0) and not markup (the detector misses it).** The def also had NO `el` where the page paints it Fire. **A notes field that is pure punctuation is a stub — treat it as absent.** |
| **notes ending in a bare wiki link** — *"Requires equipment or a status boost to block: see this section on Death."* | Ghost's **Perdition**, 2026-07-17. The link text survived; the brackets did not, so `\[\[` misses it. **A dangling "see this/that section on X" IS the tell.** |

Plus **flatly wrong prose**, which no detector will find:

- **Soul Accretion** — "Used only by Upyri". The whole family uses it.
- **Marrow Drain** — `d` said "damage + Aspir"; both the category page and Tiyanak say **"Drains MP"**.
- **Five Harpeia defs** carried a copy-pasted "Used only by Celaeno" that Podarge's and Strophadia's own
  columns refute.

The detector is §9 check 8 and is **0 file-wide**. It only finds the markup — the wrong prose needs eyes.
**The source scrape still has 11 markup defs of its own (§15), so anything imported from it must be
re-checked.**

---

### RENDER MATCHING — TAKE THE CONNECTED COMPONENT, NOT THE BOUNDING BOX. Uragnite, 2026-07-16.

Rockfin used IoU/correlation to assign three image files to three mobs, and it worked. Uragnite ran the
same tool on **infobox crops** and the first result was **contaminated**: a white-trim crop of an infobox
includes **the box's border rules**, and those straight lines dominate the mask. Every pair scored
0.69–0.94 and the real answer (identical files) was invisible.

**Fix: label the mask and keep the largest connected component** (`scipy.ndimage.label` -> `argmax` of
`ndimage.sum`), then bbox *that*. The numbers become unambiguous:

| pair | contaminated | connected-component |
|---|---|---|
| category vs Melo Melo / Shankha / Shen / Tangaroa | 0.69–0.94 | **1.000 / +1.000** (one file, reused) |
| Amphitrite vs the user's Limascabra image | — | **0.966 / +0.996** |
| Amphitrite vs any standard render | 0.40–0.49 | **0.436 / +0.285** |

The tell that a crop is border-contaminated: **every render reports the same aspect ratio** (1.6–1.75
here) and blob sizes cluster. A real render's aspect is its own.

## 6. Family stamp, kit trims, sub-types

### TWO GRIDS *DO* MAKE TWO SUB-TYPES — Uragnite, 2026-07-16. Sea Monk was the exception.

Rev 19 filed Sea Monk's two named grids **without** sub-types because the user said so. Uragnite is the
control case: same shape, opposite answer, **also from the user** — *"2 sub types uragnite and
limascabra"*. So the standing rule of this section is unchanged: **a distinct published grid earns a
sub-type; the user can override it per family.** Two data points, two directions — always ask.

| | Fire | Wind | Lit | Light | Ice | Earth | Water | Dark |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Uragnite** | 60 | 115 | **150** | 115 | 115 | 115 | 60 | 115 |
| **Limascabra** | 50 | 100 | **130** | 100 | 100 | 100 | 50 | 100 |

Damage row is all 100% on both. Limascabra is the flatter set: the same two resists dug slightly deeper,
and **none of the six weaknesses except Lightning**.

**Membership is not published anywhere.** The pages that could have carried it don't:

| source | what it gives |
|---|---|
| Shen's grid | the **Uragnite** set, Water swapped to a blue `A` -> `ab_el: ["Water"]` |
| Amphitrite's grid | damage row 100%, **every element cell `?`** — not data (§5) |
| Melo Melo / Shankha / Tangaroa | **no grid at all** |
| Adversaries table | has a **Model** column. It is **empty**. |

So it came down to the renders, and **the render comparison is a real tool when it is run correctly** —
see §5's method note (connected component, not bounding box). Amphitrite is the family's Limascabra:
the only second model, matching the user's image at **IoU 0.966**. Everything else shares one file.

**The sub-type has TWO members, and the second came from the user, not the wiki.** `aberrant uragnite`
has no page and no grid — the only thing pointing at it is its imported kit, which carries **Virulent
Haze**. Asked as (bu); the user said **yes**. So: **a mob with no published page can still be assigned
by KIT plus the user's knowledge** — the file records exactly that provenance in its notes, and it is one
field to reverse. Final: **Limascabra = amphitrite + aberrant uragnite; Uragnite = the other 16.**

**The corroboration, for the record** (not filed as data): the JP subspecies names the community tracks
list *"Limascabra (Uragnite such as Amphitrite)"* — the same naming class as **Gagana** (Roc), **Ogrebon**
(Orobon), **Boil** (Fistule), all three of which are already sub-types in this file. Monstrosity carries
exactly **Uragnite (MON) / Limascabra (MON)** — two models, matching two grids.


### !! A CATEGORY GRID NAMED AFTER ONE MEMBER — do not stamp it as the family's. Rockfin, 2026-07-16 !!

Three families running published **named** grids on the category page — Orobon (`Orobon` / `Ogrebon`),
Pteraketos (`Standard` / `Horned`), Pugil (`Pugil` / `Jagil`) — and every one of those names is a
**sub-type**. Rockfin breaks the pattern: its category publishes **exactly one grid, headed "Tchakka
Resistances"** — the name of **one of its three members**.

It is not a family grid, and the other two members prove it:

| member | resistances |
|---|---|
| **Tchakka** | the published grid |
| **Ngai** | publishes its **own** grid — Fire 5% vs Tchakka's 15%, and it **absorbs** Water where Tchakka resists it at 15% |
| **Dakuwaqa** | publishes **no grid at all** — its resistances **rotate through four HP phases** in prose |

So the grid was filed **on Tchakka alone**, Ngai got its own, and Dakuwaqa got none. **Read the grid's
header before stamping it.** A grid headed with a *sub-type* name is a sub-type grid; a grid headed with a
*mob* name is that mob's, however tempting it is to treat the category's only grid as the family default.
This is also why Rockfin has **no sub-types**: three members, three different resistance stories, and no
published sub-type name anywhere.

### !! A GRID ROW CAN PUBLISH LETTERS INSTEAD OF PERCENTAGES — Rockfin/Ngai, 2026-07-16 !!

Every resistance grid in this project has carried the legend **"A: Absorbs · S: Susceptible · R: Resists"**
under it. Until now every cell has been a percentage and the legend looked like boilerplate. **Ngai's
damage-type row is letters:**

| | Physical | Magical | Breath | Slashing | Impact | H2H | Piercing | Ranged |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Ngai** | 100% | ? | ? | **R** | **S** | **S** | **R** | **R** |

and its element row carries **`A` on Water** among the percentages.

- **`A` is storable** → `ab_el: ["Water"]`, the established field. Done.
- **`R`/`S` are NOT.** `wk`/`st` are `[[type, delta]]` and the delta vocabulary is strictly percentages
  (`+30%`, `-12.5%`, …) — the file's only non-percentage deltas are the 922 `null`s of the junk
  susceptible/resists text-list class. A letter carries **direction with no magnitude**, and inventing one
  would be exactly the fabrication the don't-guess rule exists to stop. **Routed to notes** — where Ngai's
  own General Notes say the same thing in prose anyway ("Susceptible to Blunt and Hand-to-hand damage and
  extremely resistant to other damage types"), so nothing was lost this time. **Open (bm).**

**This also nails down the row-1 order.** Ngai's `S` cells land on slots 5 and 6, and its prose names
**Blunt and Hand-to-Hand** — independently confirming the file's established damage-type order:
**Physical · Magical · Breath · Slashing · Impact · H2H · Piercing · Ranged.** (Note Impact and H2H come
*before* Piercing.)


### !! A NAMED GRID WITH NO PUBLISHED MEMBERSHIP — PARK IT. Corse, 2026-07-16 !!

Corse publishes **"Ordinary Corse Resistances"** and **"Crimson Robe Variant Resistances"** — two full
grids, both named, the damage-type row identical and the element row flipped (Light 150→50, Ice 70→30,
Dark 60→30). Uragnite's rule says that earns a sub-type.

**It doesn't, yet — because nothing published says WHICH Corse wear the crimson robe.** Uragnite's
membership was *measured* (pixel-identical renders + the user's confirmation); Corse's cannot be: the one
red-robed render in the batch is **Giltine's**, and Giltine's page publishes **no grid at all** to check
it against. **A sub-type with guessed membership is worse than no sub-type** — it stamps a wrong grid on
whoever you guessed.

**What was done:** Ordinary stamped on all 25; Crimson **parked in `family_resist_sets_pending['Corse']`**
with its provenance — the key the app ignores, first used for Peiste's Green set. Open **(ca)**; one name
from the user turns it into `family_subtypes`.

**The general shape: `family_resist_sets_pending` is where a REAL published grid waits for its
membership.** It is not a junk drawer and it is not a decision — it is a parking space with an owner.

### !! A GRID SPLIT IS NOT ALWAYS A SUB-TYPE — the user decides. Sea Monk, 2026-07-16 !!

Sea Monk's category publishes **two** grids — **"Orange and Black Resistances"** and **"White and Blue
Resistances"** — headed by the **model's colour**, which is a fourth kind of grid header (the others:
sub-type name -> Orobon/Ogrebon, Standard/Horned, Pugil/Jagil; mob name -> Tchakka; family default).

Every prior split of this shape became a sub-type. This one did not, because the user said so:

> ***"shedra types are white, image included. no sub types here, just make sure correct resist goes with
> correct color"***

So: **the two resist sets are filed per mob and `family_subtypes['Sea Monk']` does not exist.** The
mapping is his — **the four Kulushedra types (Kulushedra, Bathybic Kulushedra, Kelp Kulshedra,
Nostokulshedra) are white and blue; the other 37 are orange and black.** Nothing on the wiki says which
members are which colour: the Adversaries table has a **Model column and it is empty on every row**, and
the two grids are unlabelled beyond their colour. **Without his answer this family could not have been
filed at all** — which is the real lesson: *a colour-headed grid is unresolvable from the page alone.
Ask.*

**Do not "fix" this into sub-types later.** The rule that a distinct grid earns a sub-type (below) still
holds everywhere else; this is a documented exception with a decision behind it.

### The stamp is UNIFORM + ADDITIVE

Stamp resists + kit + crystal + job + detection on **all** members (filling members with no `ab`, keeping
extras), **then** refine notable NMs individually — their own resists / ab / sp / notes / sub / zones
override.

**But verify uniformity before assuming it:**

- **Botulus** — no family stamp at all; the category page publishes a **separate grid per mob**.
- **Slime** — three sub-types, each with its **own published category grid**.
- **Apkallu** — two models but **ONE shared grid**, headed literally *"Apkallu / Inguza Resistances"*.
- **Apkallu crystal is NOT uniform** — Lil' Apkallu's page says **Water**, not the family's Wind. The stamp
  was applied only where `crys` was absent.
- **Sandworm** — the category grid **contradicted and replaced** every old per-mob grid (Wind 85% is a
  *resist*; the import had it as a weakness).

### When a mob's own grid is PARTIAL — do not blend it with the family's

**Ongo, 2026-07-15.** Three rules already existed and they collide here:
*a '?' is not data* · *the mob's own page overrides* · *the stamp is uniform*.

Ongo's grid publishes **three cells and nothing else** — Fire 25%, Earth 30%, Dark 25% — and **all three
contradict** the Waktza category grid (50% / 70% / 70%). The other thirteen are '?'.

**Rule applied: a page that contradicts the family on every cell it publishes is telling you it is not a
family-grid mob.** Ongo was filed with its three published cells and `wk: []` — the family stamp was NOT
used to fill the thirteen unknowns, because that would assert family values for a mob whose own page just
denied them. Blending the two sources produces a grid that is true of nothing.

**The '?' rule still holds where the page says nothing at all**: Tococo, Procne and Nosoi publish grids
that are '?' *end to end*, so there is no contradiction and the family stamp stands. And where a page
publishes a **complete** grid it simply wins outright — Palila's replaces the family's.

The dividing line is **partial + contradictory**, and Ongo is the only instance so far. See open item (ag).

### Empty-list discipline

To say "this mob genuinely has NOTHING here", write an explicit `[]` (toxic tamlyn `ab=[]`, dazzling dolores
`wk=[]`) rather than removing the key — an absent key invites a future family stamp to silently refill it.

Empty **strings** are pure noise, though (`optString "" → ifBlank → null`, same as absent): 1,076 were swept
out 2026-07-15.

### Kit trims — only on clear page evidence

Stay additive unless the page shows a smaller set. Accepted triggers:

- *"Uses no TP Moves"* + Abilities column "None" → **Bedrock Barry, `ab: []`**
- *"Exclusively uses the TP move Sandspin"* → **Olgoi-Khorkhoi, `['Sandspin']`**
- *"Uses the following TP moves:"* + an explicit list → **Agathos (4)**
- *"Uses standard Apkallu TP moves (A, B, C, D). Also uses unique TP move E"* → **Isarukitsck (5)**
- The mob's **own Ability Information table** publishing a smaller set → **Hugemaw Harold (2)**,
  **Onychophora (7)**

**Additive still wins when the Listings column is LONGER:** Erinys' own table publishes 6, its Listings names
8 → keep the union of 8.

**OPEN (item j):** when the Listings column is *shorter* than the mob's own Ability table — trim or stay
additive? Dhokmak: Listings 4, own table 5 (kept 5). New evidence *for* trimming: Dyinyinga's own table
publishes 3 and both its and Nommo's Listings name exactly those 3.

### Sub-types are by RESIST SET or SKILL SET (user, 2026-07-15 — supersedes "by MODEL")

- **The criterion is data, not art:** a sub-group needs its own published grid or its own kit.
  A distinct model on its own does **not** earn a sub-type — file it as a per-mob `img` instead
  (Waktza's ongo/palila, Crab's krabkatoa). A distinct grid on its own **does**, even where the
  model is shared (Gagana was found by ONE cell: Ice 130 vs 150).
- Still true: a sub-type needs a **published wiki name** — never invent one (don't-guess rule).
  A qualifying cluster with no name stays an open question for the user.
- This RESOLVED open item (an): Barnacle Crab has a Model-column name but no distinct resists or
  skills of its own → **not a sub-type**. It reopens nothing in the 24 existing subtype sets:
  every one of them was built off its own published grid.

- Sub-type images → `assets/subtypes/`; per-mob images → `assets/mobimages/`.
- `iconForMob` (MobDb.kt) = **per-mob `img` > sub-type image (matched by sub name, ignoreCase) > family
  icon** (`mobicons/<Family>.jpg`).
- A family with **one model needs NO `family_subtypes`**.
- The browser's Type header shows "(n)" when there is >1 sub-group.
- When a base group would render as `null` alongside named subs, give the base an **explicit** sub.
- **Keep the regular type's image too** (user, 2026-07-14) — the base sub-type must also carry its model
  image.
- **GOTCHA:** giving a sub-type an `img` applies it to **every** member of that sub-group. For a colour
  subset (Crawler greens) use a **per-mob `img` override** instead.

**By-name sub-type rules are HEURISTICS — flag every edge case.** Two of thirteen were wrong on Slime
(user corrected: claret → Clot, fistule → Boil). Currently flagged: **canyon apkallu** may be an Inguza (it
lives in Marjami Ravine, exactly where the category Lore says the Inguza subspecies was rediscovered).

### Extracting a model render

Crop the top-right infobox render, keep the largest connected non-white component:

```python
nonwhite = (a.max(2) - a.min(2) > 18) | (a.min(2) < 235)
lab, n = ndimage.label(nonwhite)
big = argmax(ndimage.sum(nonwhite, lab, range(1, n+1))) + 1
```

**GOTCHA:** the thin blue page-header bar at the very top of a screenshot spans the full width and the
grabber latches onto it. Start the crop below it, and **re-check `edge-touch` on the returned bbox — if the
bbox equals the search box on any side, the blob is contaminated.** If the category render is clipped,
extract from an NM page that has a complete one (Amphiptere came from Amhuluk's page).
