## 7. Drops

Omit crafting mats (hides / tusks / ingots / meat / fangs / mandibles-as-mat) and KIs / atmas → route those
to `notes`. Keep notable gear.

**Validate every drop name against `ffxi_items.json` key `n`.**

> **NEVER conclude MISS from an exact-match test. FUZZY SUBSTRING SEARCH FIRST, AND DON'T TRUNCATE THE HIT
> LIST.** Burned 2026-07-14: wiki "Orison Seal: Body" / "Nourishing Earring" exact-missed but the DB has
> "Orison Seal: Bd." / "Nourish. Earring" → valid drops were wrongly stripped and had to be restored.
> "Odium Ring" looked absent only because a `[:4]` print truncated the hits.

> **AND SEARCH THE OTHER WORD — the DB may abbreviate the MOB'S OWN NAME inside its drop.** Wiki "Fistule
> Discharge" → DB **"Fistl. Discharge"**; `fz("Fistule")` = 0 hits, `fz("Discharge")` found it.

### Abbreviation ledger

- **Seals:** `<Job> Seal: Hd./Bd./Hn./Lg./Ft.` — Estq. / Nvrch. / Caller / Iga / Creed / Tantra / Orison /
  Bale / Unkai / Mavi / Svnt. / Ferine / Sylvan / Goetia / Aoid. / Cirque **/ Raid. (= wiki "Raider's")
  / Charis / Lncr. / Rvg.** — the last four added 2026-07-16 off Iku-Turso; that is the **complete** set
  of 20 prefixes in `ffxi_items.json`
- `Nourish. Earring`, `Jill's Spittle`, `Odyss. Chestplate`, `Subtlety Spec.`, `Estq. Earring`,
  `Tiger King Hide` (no 's), `Lu. Hide Box`, `Mahogany Htwd.`, `Amoosh.'s Tendril`, `Eschite Breast.`,
  `Phtm. Tathlum`, `Grimy Brz. Sheet`, `Fistl. Discharge`
- `Gazu Bracelets` / `Gazu Bracelets +1` — **plural**
- wiki `Arete Del Luna` → DB **`Arete del Luna`** (lowercase *del*)
- **wiki `<X> Yggzi Bead <N>` → DB `<X> Yggzi <N>`** — drop the word "Bead" (Russet Yggzi I, Phlox Yggzi IV)
- wiki `Rosette Jaseran +1` → DB **`Ros. Jaseran +1`** — the base `Rosette Jaseran` is *unabbreviated*; only
  the +1 is. **Third sighting 2026-07-16: `Demersal Degen` is unabbreviated but its +1 is `Demers. Degen
  +1`** — and **`Bathy Choker` / `Bathy Choker +1` are BOTH unabbreviated in the same drop list**, on the
  same mob (Bakunawa). **The DB abbreviates per ITEM, not per set and not per +1 rule.** Check every
  variant separately
- wiki `Kachimusha Kote +1` → DB **`Kachi. Kote +1`** — *the base `Kachimusha Kote` is unabbreviated*
  (Muut, 2026-07-16). **4th sighting of the per-item rule above.**
- wiki `Mictlantecuhtli's habit` → DB **`Mictlan. Habit`** — the mob's-own-name class (`Fistl. Discharge`)
- wiki `Zareehkl's Neckpiece` → DB **`Zrkl.'s Neckpiece`** (Zareehkl the Jubilant, Qutrub, 2026-07-17) —
  the mob's-own-name class again, and **the nastiest one yet: it drops the vowels, so the first FOUR
  letters do not survive.** `fz "Zareehkl"` returns `Zareehkl Jambiya` + `Zareehkl Scythe` and looks like a
  complete answer — the Neckpiece is simply not in that hit list. `fz "Neckpiece"` finds it at once.
  **A partial hit list is the trap: two of three drops matching does not mean the third is absent.**
- wiki `Millefleurs Sachet` → **`Mille. Sachet`**
- wiki `Ensanguined Cloth` → DB **`Ensang. Cloth`** (sluagh, Ghost, 2026-07-17). `fz "Ensanguined"` = 0;
  **`fz "Ensang"` found it.** Straight dot-abbreviation of the first word.
- wiki `Revival Tree Root` → DB **`Revival Root`** — the DB drops the MIDDLE word (`Warblade Beak's
  Coffer` → `Warblade's Coffer` class). `fz "Revival Tree Root"` = 0; `fz "Revival"` = the sole
  candidate. **Found at Doomed (rev 29), re-derived at Hound (rev 32) because it was announced in a rev
  header and never filed here.** The wiki fights itself about it inside one family: Hellion's page
  writes "Revival Tree Root", Ogama's writes "Revival Root".
- wiki `Warblade Beak's Coffer` / `Warblade Beak's Hide` → DB **`Warblade's Coffer`** / **`Warblade's
  Hide`** — the DB drops the mob's own second word (same class as `Fistl. Discharge`)
- wiki `Pigeon's Blood Ruby` → **`Pigeon's Blood`** (drops "Ruby") — sole candidate, **judgement call**
- wiki `Cleanly Snapped Rod` → DB **`Clean Snap Rod`** — a **stemming** flavour, new: the DB strips the
  inflections off *both* words (`Cleanly`->`Clean`, `Snapped`->`Snap`) rather than abbreviating with a dot.
  `fz "Cleanly Snapped"` returns nothing; **`fz "Snap"` finds it.** Search the shortest stem, not the
  wiki's word.
- **wiki `Coin of X` / `Jewel of X` / `Card of X` → DB `X Coin` / `X Jewel` / `X Card`** — a **word-order
  swap**, not an abbreviation (Sedna: wiki "Coin of Voyage" / "Jewel of Voyage" / "Coin of Ardor" /
  "Card of Ardor" -> `Voyage Coin` / `Voyage Jewel` / `Ardor Coin` / `Ardor Card`, all four already in the
  file and all four valid). `fz("Coin of")` returns a *different* set of items that really are named that
  way (Coin of Ruin, Coin of Glory…), so an exact-match miss here looks like a real absence. **Search the
  distinctive noun (`fz("Voyage")`), never the connective.**
- wiki `Suijingiri Kanemitsu` → DB **`Suijingiri KM`** — the second word reduced to **initials**, a new
  flavour again (not a dotted truncation, not stemming). `fz "Suijingiri"` finds it; `fz "Kanemitsu"` is
  0-hit. The file already stored the DB form on Tchakka, so nothing was lost.
- wiki `Mikinaak Breastplate` → DB **`Miki. Breastplate`** — and the DB carries `Mikinaak Greaves` and
  `Mikinaak Helm` **unabbreviated**. Same class as `Rosette Jaseran` / `Ros. Jaseran +1`: **the DB
  abbreviates per ITEM, not per SET.** `fz "Mikinaak"` misses it entirely; `fz "Breastplate"` finds it.

### THE ABJURATION LEDGER — solved 2026-07-16 (Pteraketos/Pakecet), **55 entries / 20 mobs, not swept**

Earlier passes noticed three of these one at a time (see the Waktza/Tulfaires line below). Pakecet's four
Body abjurations forced the general case, and it turns out to be **complete and deterministic**.

**Wiki writes `<Set> Abjuration: <Slot>`. The DB writes `<Pfx>Abjuration: <Sl.>`** — prefix abbreviated,
no space after the dot, slot abbreviated:

| slot | Head | Body | Hands | Legs | Feet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DB | `Hd.` | `Bd.` | `Hn.` | `Lg.` | `Ft.` |

| Aquarian→`A.` | Abyssal→`Ab.` | Arean→`Ar.` | Bushin→`Bu.` | Cronian→`Cr.` | Cyllenian→`Cy.` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Dryadic→`D.`** | **Earthen→`E.`** | **Grove→`Gr.`** | **Jovian→`Jo.`** | **Martial→`M.`** | **Neptunal→`N.`** |
| **Shinryu→`Sh.`** | **Triton→`Tr.`** | **Vale→`Va.`** | **Venerian→`Ve.`** | **Wyrmal→`W.`** | |

**All 85 mapped names (17 sets x 5 slots) exist in `ffxi_items.json`** — verified, no gaps.

**Why this is a ledger entry and not a guess.** The DB's 26 prefixes are *not* shortest-unique-prefix
(Aquarian gets `A.` while Abyssal gets `Ab.`), so it can't be derived by rule alone. But 16 of the 17 pair
**uniquely** by initial letters — each 2-letter prefix matches exactly one wiki name and vice versa. The
17th, `A.` = Aquarian, is ambiguous by prefix (`A.`/`Ab.`/`Ar.`) and **the file itself resolves it**:

> **`byakko` stores `A.Abjuration: Head` while `genbu` stores `Aquarian Abjuration: Head`** — the same
> item, in both forms, on two records. A Rosetta stone sitting in our own data.

**THE DEBT: 55 invalid abjuration drop entries across 20 mobs** still use the wiki long form — `amymone`,
`asida`, `aspidochelone`, `bia`, `byakko` (mixed — half converted!), `emputa`, `genbu`, `hanbi`,
`kammavaca`, `khon`, `khun`, `ma`, `met`, `naphula`, `peirithoos`, `ruea`, `sava savanovic`, `suzaku`,
`wasserspeier`, `yilan`. Every one currently renders a drop the item DB cannot resolve. **Pakecet's own
four were filed in the correct DB form during this pass; the other 20 mobs are untouched** per
"only touched families cleaned". This is the cheapest, safest sweep on the board — the mapping is a lookup
table, not an inference. Open **(bf)**.

**NEW FLAVOUR, 2026-07-16 (Orobon/Cirein-croin) — WORD-ORDER INVERSION. The DB does not always abbreviate;
sometimes it REVERSES the name.** Wiki `Jewel of Balance` → DB **`Balance Jewel`**; `Stone of Balance` →
**`Balance Stone`**; `Stone of Wieldance` → **`Wieldance Stone`**; `Card of Wieldance` → **`Wieldance Card`**.
Every one is a 0-hit substring miss on the full wiki name and a 0-hit miss on the *leading* word too — only
the per-word fallback in `fz.py` finds them, and only because it searches **every** word. A truncation-only
mental model would have stripped four valid drops. Also here: wiki `Cirein-croin's Lantern` → DB
**`Cirein. Lantern`** (the mob's-own-name class, `Fistl. Discharge`); wiki `Delectable Orobon Steak` → DB
**`D. Oro. Steak`** (three initialisms in one name — `fz("Delectable")` and `fz("Orobon")` both miss it;
only `fz("Steak")` finds it).

New, 2026-07-15 (Waktza / Tulfaires): `Souveran Schaller +1` → **`Souv. Schaller +1`**;
`Abyssal Abjuration: Legs` → **`Ab.Abjuration: Lg.`**; `Bushin Abjuration: Head` → **`Bu.Abjuration: Hd.`**;
`Cronian Abjuration: Head` → **`Cr.Abjuration: Hd.`**; `Phlox Yggzi Bead III` → **`Phlox Yggzi III`**;
`Phlox Yggrete Shard III` → **`P. Ygg. Shard III`**. Abjurations are filed as the abjuration, not as the
gear they trade for.

## 8. Zones

`zones = List<[zone, "lv-range"?]>` per mob, so OmniWatch can answer "mob in zone = Lv A-B".

**This is STORAGE for ALL mobs, standard and NM.** The card's "Zones" row is display-gated to `mob.nm`, but
that is **display-only**. User-confirmed 2026-07-14: keep filling zones for standard mobs too — don't stop
tracking them just because the app hides them.

Source from the wiki's Adversaries / Listings / Event-Appearances tables **as text**. Don't fabricate. The
**Adversaries table is the level authority** for regular mobs — align each mob's `lv` to it. **BUT DO NOT
NARROW `lv` TO THE ADVERSARIES SPAN — Pugil, 2026-07-16.** The table only prints levels for *some* rows
(`[S]` rows are usually blank), and event appearances are on a different table entirely. The file's `lv` is
already **the union across every appearance**, and it is real data:

- `pugil` `[1,17]` = the exact union of its four table rows **including the `[S]` row's 14-17**. That is the
  proof: the import was unioning the table, `[S]` rows and all.
- `pug pugil` `[4,64]` — the table's printed rows only reach 10, and its four `[S]` rows are level-blank.
  The 64 is a **Grauberg [S]** Pug Pugil, and Grauberg [S] is a level-60s zone.
- `giant pugil` `[9,75]` / `puffer pugil` `[13,77]` — table maxes 20 and 18. Both are on the **Event
  Appearances** table (Ilrusi Atoll, Assault), which is where the 70s come from.

Narrowing any of those to the Adversaries span would have destroyed real levels. **Put the per-zone range
in the `zones` row — that is what `zones` is for — and leave `lv` alone** unless a mob's OWN page publishes
a level (a single-zone NM: Serra `[44,46]`->`[49,50]`, Buburimboo `[30,80]`->`[30,31]`, Swamfisk
`[11,80]`->`[10,11]` — those 80s were junk, and the page beats everything).

### Zone-name canon

`zones.json` is authoritative; the app normalizes apostrophes / hyphens / brackets. **Store the apostrophe
form** for nicer display ("The Shrine of Ru'Avitau", "King Ranperre's Tomb", "Pso'Xja", "Fei'Yin").

Gotchas:
- `Abyssea-Attohwa`, `Abyssea-Misareaux` — **no spaces** around the hyphen
- `Dynamis-Tavnazia` — no spaces
- `West Sarutabaruta [S]`, `Meriphataud Mountains [S]`, `Sauromugue Champaign [S]`
- `Escha ZiTah` — **no apostrophe, no hyphen** (the wiki writes "Escha - Zi'Tah")
- `Valley of Sorrows`
- **U-zones use the [S]-style bracket:** `Yorcia Weald [U]`, `Cirdas Caverns [U]`

**Free text** (no `zones.json` entry) — established forms:
`Sheol A` / `Sheol B` / `Sheol C` / `Sheol - Gaol`; `Ninth Walk`; `Maquette Abdhaljs-Legion`; the Einherjar
chambers (`Helmwige's` / `Schwertleite's` / `Waltraute's` / `Grimgerde's` / `Rossweisse's` / `Siegrune's
Chamber`).

### The ferries — **no "Ferry - X/Y" string is a zone. THREE different boats, and they are easy to mix up.**

Each wiki ferry maps to **two** zone rows, one per leg. Expanded 2026-07-16 (Sea Monk) — the old line here
covered only the Silver Sea and **would have put the Mhaura/Al Zahbi mobs on the wrong boat**:

| wiki writes | store these two rows | already used by |
|---|---|---|
| **Ferry - Mhaura/Selbina** | `Ship bound for Mhaura` + `Ship bound for Selbina` | ocean crab, sea crab, ocean pugil, sea pugil, pirate pugil |
| **Ferry - Mhaura/Al Zahbi** | **`Open sea route to Al Zahbi` + `Open sea route to Mhaura`** | gugru crab, gugru jagil, gugru orobon, ocean jagil, passage crab, northern/southern piranu |
| **Ferry - Nashmau/Al Zahbi** | `Silver Sea route to Nashmau` + `Silver Sea route to Al Zahbi` | apkallu, abyssal pugil, cyan deep crab/pugil, submarine nipper, orobon (nm) |

All six names are in `zones.json` (region **Ferries**). **The Silver Sea is the NASHMAU boat; the Mhaura
boat is the Open sea route.** `Manaclipper` is a zone in its own right and needs no expansion.

A whole-file U-zone normalization sweep ran 2026-07-14; re-run its group-by-stripped-key verifier after
adding zones.

## 9. Verifiers — run all of these after every edit

```python
# 1. null poison (§4) — THE critical one
assert not [k for m in d['mobs'].values() for k,v in m.items() if v is None]
assert not [k for k,v in d['abilities'].items() if v is None]

# 2. ab_el must be a list, ability el must not be
assert not [k for k,v in mobs.items() if isinstance(v.get('ab_el'), str)]
for k,v in abils.items(): assert not isinstance(v.get('el'), list), k

# 3. undefined ability refs (family-scoped while working a family)
und = sorted({a for k in FAM for a in (mobs[k].get('ab') or []) if a not in abils})
assert not und, und

# 4. drops vs ffxi_items.json  — NOTE the known-DB-gap exemption
bad = [(k,x) for k in FAM for x in (mobs[k].get('drops') or '').split(', ')
       if x and x not in ITEM_NAMES and 'Chapter' not in x]
assert not bad, bad

# 5. zones vs zones.json (strip-normalized), minus the free-text set
strip = lambda s: re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', s.lower())
bz = {z[0] for k in FAM for z in (mobs[k].get('zones') or [])
      if strip(z[0]) not in ZONES_NORM and z[0] not in FREE_ZONES}

# 6. spells vs jobs.json spellinfo
bs = {s for k in FAM for s in (mobs[k].get('sp') or []) if s not in SPELLS}

# 7. malformed glued name+condition entries
mal = [(k,x) for k in FAM for x in (mobs[k].get('ab') or []) + (mobs[k].get('sp') or [])
       if re.search(r'[a-z][A-Z]', x)]

# 8. wiki markup leaking into ability text  (see §12)
mk = [k for k,v in abils.items() if re.search(r'__NOTOC|===|\{\{|\[\[|File:', str(v.get('d','')) + str(v.get('notes','')))]

# 8b. ...and into MOB notes — Rockfin found 2 survivors of an earlier pass of my own
mkm = [k for k,v in mobs.items() if v.get('notes') and re.search(r'\[\[|\]\]|link=', json.dumps(v['notes']))]

# 9. mob notes must be a LIST, never a bare string (§4) — Rockfin, 2026-07-16
assert not [k for k,v in mobs.items() if 'notes' in v and not isinstance(v['notes'], list)]
```

**`audit.py` (shipped alongside this doc) runs all of the above file-wide plus the §11 numbers.**
Run `python3 audit.py [assets_path]` and update §11 after any data change.

`fz.py` = fuzzy item search — use it before ever concluding a drop is absent.

**`gen_template.py` IS STILL LOST** and needs rebuilding before the next MobTemplate export.

**Enhancing 38** · Buff 32 · **Ranged 16** · **Gaze 11** · Special 3 · Healing 3 · + one-offs
`Enhancing/Healing`, `Offensive`, `Frontal Cone`, `AoE` (the last three are *areas*, not types).

**Crystal:** Water 932 · Earth 917 · Fire 750 · Wind 722 · Dark 662 · Light 240 · Ice 217 · Lightning 190
· **Thunder 61 — the same crystal under a second name** · junk: `N` 17, lowercase fire/earth/dark/water/ice
24, `None` 7, `Fire Lightning` 3, `Element` 2, `Dark or Earth` 1, `Varies` 1. A Thunder→Lightning merge
plus case normalisation is cheap.

**Detection:** Sight 3,471 · Sound 3,357 · Scent 1,098 · True Sight 1,014 · Magic 660 · **Blood 510**
(= low-HP detection, and they are the undead families) · True Sound 70 · **JA 57** (see open item (f) and
§15 — `JA` came straight from the scrape's `detect_flags`).

### Data-quality landmines found by reading existing defs

An existing def is **not** a trustworthy def — five flavours of leaked wiki markup and three cases of
flatly wrong prose have been caught so far. **See §5 for the table**; the detector is §9 check 8 and is 0
file-wide.

### The 31-spell junk `sp` list — and it is a whole family of stamps

The identical 31-spell block (`Fire V / Blizzard V / … / Sleepga II`) is on **108 mobs**, byte-identical —
not the 3 first spotted. It is one of a set of job+level-tier import stamps: **108×** the 31-spell BLM-V
block · **37×** a 32-spell BLM-IV · **36×** a 32-spell WHM · **35×** the 6-spell PLD block (Cure IV / Holy
/ Banish / Protect / Shell / Flash) · **34×** another 32-spell · **29×** an 11-spell NIN block. Some are
*right* (a Kindred Black Mage really does cast that); some are absurd (a Lv 94-96 flume toad with all six
Ancient Magic). Detector: group by `tuple(sp)` and read the top counts. **Left as found everywhere** — a
page has to contradict before it is touched.

### (bj) **PUGIL — do Jagils use Recoil Dive INSTEAD OF Screwdriver, or as well? — ASKED, UNANSWERED.**
The file's own imported note on Recoil Dive claims Jagils use it *instead of* Screwdriver — a **swap**. The
category ability table does **not** say that: it gates only the Recoil Dive row ("Jagil types and NMs
only") and leaves Screwdriver ungated, so **additive** is what the standing rule ("stay additive unless
the page shows a smaller set") gives, and that is what was stamped — all 22 Jagils carry both.

**But nothing published contradicts the swap either, and three things fit it:**
- `hrosshvalur` — its Listings Abilities column publishes **Aqua Ball / Counterspore / Recoil Dive**. No
  Screwdriver.
- `divagating jagil` — `ab` is **Aqua Ball / Recoil Dive**. No Screwdriver. (Import-inherited, not
  page-verified.)
- **No mob anywhere in the family publishes both moves.**

Against: both of those are *short* lists that may just be naming notable moves, and imported def prose has
been wrong before (which is why the rule exists). **Held as additive + flagged rather than acted on.** One
Jagil page with a full Abilities column settles it.

   were the answer, not noise.
2. **Absent is not false** (§4's shape, one field over): `optBoolean("agg", false)` renders a missing key
   as "not aggressive", so *passive* and *never recorded* are the same bytes. A sweep is not undoable from

### (bw) URAGNITE — the live category page and the screenshot DISAGREE. Which revision is ours?

While answering the Limascabra question I fetched `bg-wiki.com/ffxi/Category:Uragnite` directly. **Both
grids match the screenshot cell for cell** — but the rest of the page does not:

| | the user's screenshot (what I filed) | the live fetch |
|---|---|---|
| ability table | **6 rows**, Virulent Haze present with its Condition | **5 rows — no Virulent Haze** |
| columns | `Ability · Y' · Area · Target · Type · shadows · Condition` | adds a **`Class`** column, splitting category from element |
| General Notes | 40-second shell timer, the HP/10 threshold, 9 ticks, 1%/tick regen, **Despoil** | rewritten and shorter; adds **"Will retaliate with Gas Shell if physically attacked while inside its shell"** |
| Bestiary box | has a **Japanese** row (ウラグナイト) | no Japanese row |

Both are `From FFXI Wiki`, same URL. **The user left this one to my judgement. What I filed:**

| the live page's difference | call | why |
|---|---|---|
| adds *"Will retaliate with Gas Shell if physically attacked while inside its shell"* | **FILED**, in `family_notes` and in Gas Shell's def, **with the provenance written into the note** | it is *what the move is for*, abilities are priority #1, and **nothing contradicts it** — the screenshot's notes are silent, and blank is not "no" (§5). Amphitrite's own page corroborates the pattern: it counters with Virulent Haze after absorbing damage |
| **drops** Virulent Haze from the ability table | **IGNORED** | removal is not a correction. The screenshot has the row, Amphitrite and Tangaroa use the move, and Tangaroa's page names it. Deleting on a blank would lose real data |
| **drops** the Despoil / 40s / threshold / regen bullets | **IGNORED** — kept the screenshot's | superset beats subset when they do not conflict |
| adds a **`Class`** column | noted only | it is the wiki catching up: `Class` = the category circle, `Type` = the element — **exactly the split this project reverse-engineered from icon colours**. If it lands everywhere, §5's colour-matching becomes a text read |

**The rule this sets: a directly-fetched page is corroboration, not a source.** It can *add* a fact that
nothing contradicts, with its provenance written into the record; it cannot *delete* one. Everything
filed this way is one line to strip. **A fresh shot of the category page still settles it.**

## 14. UI state (AuctionApp.kt / MobDb / AuctionViewModel)

`ui.mobView` is a **plain String** (`all` / `family` / **`zone`**) — no enum, so a new mode needs **no
ViewModel change**. It is listed in **two** pickers and both must be patched: AuctionApp.kt ~line 308 (the
browser) and ~2969 (Settings "default view", pref `defMobView` via `vm.setDefaultMobView`).

**View = Family:**
Ecosystem (**RED** GroupHeader) → Type (**GOLD** SubGroupHeader, "(n)" when >1 sub) → Sub-type (**ORANGE**
`0xFFE8912D`) → MobRow.

Sub-group = `typeMobs.groupBy { it.sub ?: type }`; single-base types skip the sub-type level.

**View = Zone** — added rev 10. User: *"in view, i want a zone view that sorts mobs by zone. with that i
can see what we are missing as well."*

Zone (GroupHeader) → Family (SubGroupHeader) → MobRow. `zoneNested` is built beside `nested` and the
LazyColumn branches zone-then-family.

- **A mob is listed under EVERY zone in its `zones` list**, so the item key must be `"$zone|${it.key}"` —
  the mob key alone is **not** unique in this view.
- Zones sort alphabetically, but **`NO_ZONE`** (a top-level const, `"— No zone data"`) is **pinned last**
  via a `LinkedHashMap` so the ~5,126 zoneless mobs never bury the real data. That bucket **is** the to-do
  list — it is grouped by family, so it reads directly as "which family needs an Adversaries shot".
- **`MobRow(vm, mob, inZone: String? = null)`** — the 3rd arg is new. Under a zone header it shows
  `NM · Lv <that zone's range>` (from `mob.zones.firstOrNull { it.first == inZone }?.second`, falling back
  to `levelText`) instead of family + level, since the family is already the sub-header.

**Mob card** — collapsible boxes:
- **Details:** detect / job / resp / crys / spawn / drops / ResistGrid (green = weak, red = resist,
  **blue = Abs**, muted = neutral) / immune / absorb. Icon is sub-aware; eco shows under the type title.
  **Zones USED TO BE DOCUMENTED HERE AS "[NM only]" AND IT WAS NEVER TRUE OF THIS BUILD** — `MobDetailScreen`
  had no zone row at all when rev 30 went looking for it. Both this doc and the notes claimed a row the
  code did not have. **Verify a documented UI element against the source before "moving" it.**
- **Zones** (rev 30, USER: *"i want a new, collapseable section(defaults as collapsed) under abilities in
  each card named Zones... if we do not have zone info, keep the section but leave it blank, it will help
  me to know what we still need to fill in"*) — sits **between Abilities and Spells**, and is the one
  section that is **ALWAYS rendered, unconditionally**: no `isNotEmpty()` gate, no NM gate. An empty card
  is the point — it is the per-mob to-do marker, the card-level twin of the Zone view's `NO_ZONE` bucket.
  Rows come from `MobZoneRow(zone, levels, showDivider)` — **named `MobZoneRow` because `ZoneRow(vm, zone:
  Zone)` ALREADY EXISTS at ~line 250** for the zone browser; the overload would have compiled but the clash
  is a trap. Level range renders right-aligned in gold, `"Lv "`-prefixed only when it starts with a digit
  (the `LevelRow` idiom), and is omitted when null.
  **GOTCHA: `CollapsibleSection` keys its saved state on the TITLE ALONE** (`rememberSaveable(key =
  "collapse_$title")`), so expanding Zones on one mob expands it on every mob. That is pre-existing
  behaviour shared by Details/Abilities/Spells — not new, but now it applies to a section that renders on
  all 6,733 mobs.
- **Abilities** (type · element) · **Spells** · **General Notes** · user **Notes**

`parsePctDelta` returns a String and handles decimals.
Card General Notes = `mob.notes + subtypeNotes + familyNotes` (`.distinct()`).
`Mob.image` field and the `"img"` parser are wired.

**Kotlin cannot be compiled in this environment** — verify any property/arity against the actual source
before referencing it.

## 15. The source scrape — `mob_individuals.json`

**This is the file mobs.json was built from.** The user re-uploaded it 2026-07-15 and asked for a
read-only diff; **nothing was changed**. 11.7 MB. `_meta`: `schema_version` 5, `entry_count` 6733, cleaned
2026-05-13, inputs `mob_individuals2.json` + `mob_abilities.json`, `abilities_scraped` 1204,
`ability_details` 1097. Three sections: `individuals` (6,733), `ability_details` (1,097),
`family_abilities` (209).

**Read this section before planning any big sweep.** It changes what several of the scary numbers in §11
actually mean.

### The two findings that matter most

**1. The 4,829 undefined ability refs are a STRING FIX, not missing data.**
Zero of our 142 undefined names are in the source — because the source's *def* names are clean; the glue
happened in `individuals[*].abilities`. **Strip the trailing `(condition)` and 36 names / 3,763 refs — 78%
— land on defs we already have.** Only **106 names / 1,066 refs** are defined nowhere: Goblin Rush 254,
Dimensional Death 142, Barbed Crescent 141, Quadrastrike 110, Everyone's Grudge 63, Smite of Rage 49,
Hydro Shot 48… The Leech pass is the template; no new scrape is needed for the 78%.

**2. `modifiers` has only 12 keys — and it explains the entire resist pass.**
`slashing, piercing, h2h, impact` + the 8 elements. **No Physical, no Magical, no Breath, no Ranged.** The
source *physically cannot express half the BG grid*, which is why every old family stamp was wrong the same
way and only ever carried those four damage types. **750 of our mobs now carry a Physical/Magical/Breath/
Ranged cell that could not have come from the import** — Slime 93, Bat 77, Mandragora 57, Bee 56, Fly 54,
Lesser Bird 52, Flock Bat 52, Greater Bird 36, plus Craklaw's Magical 112.5, Frog's Magical 75, Harpeia's
Breath 75. Every one of those was read off a grid image. **The screenshot pass is not redundant work — it
is the only way this data can exist.**

### What the source has that we should take

| | |
|---|---|
| **`individuals[*].type` IS the ecosystem** | on **4,477 mobs**, and it covers **128 of our 129 eco-less families**. Beastmen 743 · Undead 431 · Vermin 388 · Arcana 366 · Amorphs 300 · Birds 291 · Aquans 288 · Plantoids 247 · Beasts 216 · Demons 201 · Lizards 160 · Dragons 156 · Unclassified 153 · Elementals 126 · Empty 56 · Archaic Machines 47 · Luminians 33 · Vorageans 33 … **41 distinct values.** Needs singular/plural normalisation (Plantoid 49 / Amorph 25 / Demon 25 / Aquan 17 …) and junk dropped (Hill Lizard, Diremite, Manticore, Amoeban, Wyvern = *family* names in the type slot; lowercase `plantoid`; `Cutscene NPC`). **This is `family_eco` for the whole rest of the project, pre-scraped.** |
| **`family_abilities`** | 209 families → kit lists, **995 distinct ability names**. **29 families that have ZERO `ab` in our file have a published kit here**: cardian (54 mobs), imp (40), caturae (31), poroggo (24), soulflayer (19), vampyr (19), cluster (16), khimaira (16), gargouille (15), bugbear (14), orcish warmachine (13), qutrub (13)… Junk keys exist (`:category:craklaws`). |
| **521 ability defs we don't have** | and **434 of them are exactly what `family_abilities` needs**. Of the 995 names: 548 defined in our file, **434 only in the source**, 13 nowhere. Kits *and* defs for the unprocessed beastman/demon/arcana families are already scraped and waiting. Def fields: `name/family/type/range/utsusemi/dispel/notes/description` (1,048 of 1,097 have a description). |

### Fields the import never took

`traits` (43 mobs — Double Attack 9, Store TP 6, Fast Cast 5, Triple Attack 5, Auto Regen, Counter, Attack
Bonus, Enparalyze, Enwater, Defense Bonus, High Magic Evasion, Regain). **We have been hand-typing these
into `notes` off the pages — aquarius, tegmine, wanda — and 12 of the 43 already carry our notes.**

`susceptible` (1,944) + `resists` (1,406) as **text lists**, separate from `modifiers`, with vocabulary our
grid cannot hold: `Piercing damage`, `Blunt Damage`, **`Dark Earth`**, **`Varies`**. This is where the junk
stamps came from.

`immunities` (489, **numeric**, alongside the `immune` list of 420 — Drain 275 / Aspir 275 / Dark Sleep 120
/ Sleep 65) · `job` (1,628, **numeric**, alongside `main_job`/`sub_job`) · `absorbs` (5) · **`detect_flags`
= 8 booleans including `ja`** — which is the origin of open item (f)'s `det=['Sight','JA']`.

### The markup leak is the scraper's, not ours

The source's Diffusion Ray `description` is literally `File:Diffusion Ray.png`. **The source has 11 such
defs** — Beak Lunge, Blood Drain, Diffusion Ray, Nature's Meditation, Oblivion Smash, Rail Cannon, Rending
Deluge, Restoral, Tempestuous Upheaval, Virulent Haze, Wing Slap. **We are at 0 file-wide**, having fixed
every one that reached us — and **our Nature's Meditation and Tempestuous Upheaval are *better* than the
source's** (real descriptions vs `File:` markup). The page beats the scrape, proven. **If the 521 defs are
ever imported, Rail Cannon and Restoral bring their markup with them — run the §9 detector on the import.**

### We are ahead everywhere we have worked

`ab` non-empty: **4,129 vs 3,185** (+948 from family stamps). **Only 3 mobs have abilities in the source
and none in ours — bedrock barry, erle, sargas — i.e. exactly our 3 deliberate page-backed `ab: []`.**

**The source has no field at all for:** zones (1,607) · notes (619) · sub (817) · img (220) · drops (1,532)
· spawn (1,882) · nmlv (898) · ab_el (29) · family_notes (80) · family_subtypes (24) · family_eco (82) ·
family_icons (201). All of that is ours.

### Roster

6,733 both. **4 names differ.** Source-only: **`belladonna`** (our deliberate delete, the orphan dup) and
**`cerberus (notorious monster)`** — *not* a documented delete, **reconcile this**. Ours-only:
**`lamie no.19`** (fam Lamiae) and **`warder partisan`** (fam Yagudo). Note the source carries *both*
spacings of the Lamie NMs (`lamie no 7` **and** `lamie no.7`).
